Organise and manage the diverse range of daily tasks, routines and administrative duties which teachers are required to undertake in the classroom and school-wide context
incompatibilities: must not have completed EDUC3086 Professional Experience 3 - Informed Planning (HP) at the University of South Australia

title: Space Vehicle Design
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course aims to impart students with the knowledge and skills essential for air vehicle, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and space vehicle design, covering topics such as vehicle weight calculation, mission fuel weight estimation, sensitivity analysis, standard requirements compliance, vehicle design parameters determination, overall configuration design, and system selection and integration. Upon completion, learners will master the conceptual design of various aerospace vehicles and develop a comprehensive understanding of the design cycle specific to this domain. Graduates will be equipped to meet the design requirements of aerospace vehicles, contributing significantly to the aerospace industry.
learning_outcomes: Explain design phases of aerospace vehicles such as aircrafts, UAVs and space vehicles
Perform conceptual design of different types of aerospace vehicles
Explain the parameters that influence the design of aerospace vehicles
Explain the method of design tasks and technical reports in a report in a group
Use analytical and numerical methods to solve aerospace vehicle design problems
prerequisites: must have completed all of ENGA4000 Astrodynamics/ENGAX200 Aeronautical Engineering/ENGM2005 Fluid Mechanics/ENGM3002 Mechanical Systems and Design Project

title: Aerospace Propulsion
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with the knowledge and skills required to analyse air and non-air breathing propulsion systems, encompassing gas turbines, ramjets, ducted rockets, scramjets, and space propulsion. Through studying combustion reactions, specific fuel consumption, and aerothermodynamics of various components, learners will develop critical thinking and problem-solving abilities to optimise gas turbine component design parameters. By mastering thrust prediction and engine performance, students will gain practical insights into the complexities of propulsion systems. Graduates will emerge equipped to address real-world challenges in gas turbine design within the aerospace industry, contributing significantly to technological advancement.
learning_outcomes: Explain working principles of air breathing and non-air breathing propulsion systems such as turbojets, turbofans, ramjets, scramjets and rockets
Demonstrate skills to analytically and numerically solve problems relating to aerospace propulsion systems
Demonstrate ability to write and present aerospace propulsion design results and data in a report independently
Demonstrate ability to write and present aerospace propulsion design results and data in a report in a group
Explain the parameters that influence the performance of gas turbine engines

title: Electromagnetic Engineering
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course builds up on electro- and magneto-statics to complete the foundations of electromagnetic theory by including time-varying phenomena. As such, the course focusses on electrodynamic fields and waves, with their applications in electrical and electronic engineering. Topics include: Brief review of electrostatics and magnetostatics, electric and magnetic fields in materials, Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, capacitance and inductance in circuit models, differential and integral forms of Maxwell's equations, boundary field conditions, electromagnetic waves, scattering of plane waves from media boundaries, guided-waves and transmission lines, radiation, antenna fundamentals, propagation of electromagnetic waves.
learning_outcomes: Interpret Maxwell’s equations of electromagnetics in integral and differential forms
Understand the properties of conductors, dielectrics and magnetic materials
Employ vector calculus to solve static, quasistatic and dynamic electromagnetics problems
Formulate electromagnetic waves to explain propagation, reflection, and refraction
prerequisites: Must have completed all of ENGE2002 Signals and Systems/ENGI2001 Engineering Modelling 2

title: Instructional Leadership
syllabus_overview: This course aims to introduce students to the theories of instructional leadership through evidence-based approaches to teaching and learning leadership. Students will explore current leadership theories related to leading learning and teaching and how to lead for assessment, measurement, and evaluation. Furthermore, students will explore how to interrogate evidence for learning and teaching to develop strategies to enhance learning and teaching outcomes. These aims will be contextualised in schools and education systems to develop approaches to improving student learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Understand current theories and research on learning and teaching
Critique instructional leadership practice and processes
Evaluate how instructional leadership can create change in diverse education settings

title: Curriculum and Policy for First Nations Education
syllabus_overview: To develop informed and critical understandings of the curriculum, policies, theories and practices of ‘First Nations education’ with a focus on Culturally Responsive Pedagogies for teachers and leaders of learning. Curriculum construction is not neutral and is power laden. In this course we critically consider how curriculum and policy in Australia is entangled with ongoing coloniality. To develop critical understanding and appropriate policy and curriculum content knowledge required by leaders and teachers to engage Aboriginal students, and to teach all students about Aboriginal histories, cultures, and languages as required by the Australian Curriculum, Early Years Learning Framework and AITSL’s Professional Standards for Teachers 1.4 and 2.4.
learning_outcomes: Explain the knowledge and skills required to work effectively with diverse Aboriginal learners, families, peoples, perspectives, and histories
Explain and justify assessment, curriculum and evidence-based pedagogical practices relevant to Aboriginal education
Interpret knowledge of culturally responsive teaching that respects and values the democratic rights of Aboriginal children and the sovereignties of Aboriginal First Nations through education
Critically analyse the contested nature of curriculum and policy in critical curriculum studies and education literature

title: Culturally Responsive Pedagogy in First Nations Education
syllabus_overview: To prepare teachers and leaders to drive change in Australian schooling by examining and enacting theory in Culturally Responsive Pedagogy (CRP) that prioritises First Nations Educational Sovereignty. The course aims to: 1) Develop learners’ appreciation of POSITIONALITY through awareness of the ways in which individuals’ locations in society shape what they see. 2) Enhance learners’ awareness of POWER, and how Australian school curriculum and pedagogy constitute spaces for the renegotiation of power. 3) Deepen learners’ appreciation of PLACE for enabling students to connect what they are learning to their lived realities, communities, and Country. Workshops immerse learners in these big picture ideas and their micro-level manifestations through CRPs that are characertised by teaching that is: intellectually demanding; connected to lifeworlds; activist-oriented; multi-modal; socio-politically informed; place-based; dialogic; and world-facing.
learning_outcomes: Apply culturally responsive pedagogical theory and skills to work effectively with diverse Aboriginal learners, families, peoples, and perspectives
Draw on evidence based research to explain how culturally responsive pedagogies can lead toward positive outcomes for Aboriginal students

Apply culturally responsive pedagogical theories to the design of purposeful, localised learning experiences centred around First Nations perspectives and responsive to local student and community contexts

title: Mentoring for Leadership
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop understandings of quality models of mentoring across all levels of education.
learning_outcomes: Analyse contemporary theories of mentoring and its application to leadership
Critique the strengths and limitations of theories of mentoring and its application to leadership
Evaluate the application of theories of mentoring and its application to leadership in diverse contexts
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7060 or EDUC7060L Mentoring for Teachers at the University of Adelaide

title: Electronic Devices and Circuits
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: The course aims to provide students with an in-depth understanding of semiconductor materials and properties, electronic components and their applications. Students learn to analyse, design, and troubleshoot electronic circuits using devices like diodes, Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs), Field-Effect Transistors (FETs), and operational amplifiers through theoretical study and practical exercises. Students will also gain knowledge and skills on common stages of amplifiers. The emphasis is on real-world applications, preparing students for further studies or careers in electronics and related fields.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the fundamental principles and characteristics of semiconductor devices including diodes, transistors, and operational amplifiers to predict their behaviour in electronic circuits.
Design and evaluate diode-based circuits for different applications, including logic gates, rectification, clipping, filtering, and voltage regulation using p-n junction principles.

Analyse bipolar junction transistors (BJT) circuits using appropriate DC and small-signal AC models and evaluate their performance as amplifiers through theoretical calculations and practical measurements.

Understand field-effect transistor (FET) physics and types, and design and analyse metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) amplifier circuits to meet specified performance requirements, using appropriate DC and small-signal AC models and circuit analysis techniques.
Design, analyse and troubleshoot operational amplifier circuits for practical applications, considering practical limitations and performance specifications.
Identify and evaluate power amplifier configurations and output stages based on efficiency, power requirements, and distortion specifications to select appropriate solutions for given applications.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of ENGE1000 Electrical and Electronic Systems/ENGI1003 Engineering Physics/ENGI1004 Engineering Modelling 1

title: Assessment and Evaluation
syllabus_overview: To critique and contribute to contemporary understanding of effective assessment, evaluation and managing learning, and to build advanced insight into the development learning communities that are ethically, socially and professionally sustainable in a lifelong learning perspective.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a deep understanding of research-based conceptions of assessment
Engage in advanced problem-solving skills in inter-related fields of assessment and learning practices
Demonstrate the effect of personal and professional ethical actions, and the implication for planning, practice and evaluation of processes and outcomes
Critically apply knowledge of effective learning processes and structures of power to a number of educational cases inside and outside the school
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7553 Assessment and Evaluation at the University of Adelaide

title: Professional Experience 3: Inquiry into Practice (Junior Primary)
syllabus_overview: This course aims to support pre-service teachers to extend and transform their practices as they engage in cycles of planning, teaching, assessing, reflecting and appraising during their final placement.
learning_outcomes: Collect, interpret and use a range of data when planning for teaching and learning and when making adjustments to teaching and assessment practices
Apply the official curriculum, other resources and knowledge of prior learning to design connected teaching and learning sequences and effective assessments
Differentiate planning and teaching to meet the needs of all learners
Critically analyse and evaluate pedagogical and assessment decisions, and the progress of student learning, with reference to literature and theory
Maintain a safe and inclusive learning environment over a sustained time
prerequisites: must have completed all of EDUC5908 Professional Experience 1: Infant and Toddler Pedagogies Practices/EDUC6900 Professional Experience 2: Preschool Pedagogies and Practices

title: Leading Australian First Nations Education
syllabus_overview: The core focus is to prepare school leaders and teachers to lead change in diverse Aboriginal contexts by examining local, national and international education research evidence in culturally responsive pedagogies. Drawing upon Critical leadership Studies, Australian Aboriginal education theory and culturally responsive pedagogical theoretical frameworks, the course investigates how Indigenous peoples maintain and revitalize local languages and cultural knowledges as they relate to teaching and learning. Students will acquire knowledge of culturally responsive leadership approaches for appropriate teaching and learning practices that include: rejecting deficit views of learners, setting high expectations of teachers with a commitment to all student’s success; engages multiple knowledges and multiple literacies; leadership support for teachers classroom practices that validates student’s culture; school systems and structures that bridges gaps between school and home; commitment to whole school approach to culturally responsive instructional strategies. A key focus is to ensure equity and diversity and that social exclusion in education is addressed via building school structures and cultures that engages and support the identities, knowledges and epistemologies of Aboriginal students and the local community.This focus is aimed at addressing Australian inequity for a positive national future.
learning_outcomes: Explain the knowledge and skills required to work effectively with diverse Aboriginal learners, families, peoples, perspectives, and histories
Explain and justify assessment, curriculum and evidence-based pedagogical practices relevant to Aboriginal education
Interpret knowledge of culturally responsive teaching that respects and values the democratic rights of Aboriginal children and the sovereignties of Aboriginal First Nations through education
Critically analyse the contested nature of educational leadership in leadership studies in education literature
Examine international case studies in educational leadership to ascertain how contemporary policy affects educational leaders

title: Engineering Associate Engagement with Professional Practice
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to provide learners with direct exposure to the engineering field through structured, real-world engagements. This immersive experience reinforces theoretical knowledge with the practical application of engineering concepts, tools, and practices. The course focuses on learners reflecting on their engagement with professional practice, which includes in-curricular, extra-curricular, and in-industry experiences, and how these have helped them develop and apply the Engineers Australia Stage 1 Competencies of a engineering associate It links academic learning with life and industry experiences, deepening understanding of engineering challenges and solutions, and prepares learners to become engineering associates.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to perform engineering tasks under supervision using appropriate methods, tools, and techniques across areas such as operations, facilities, and design, and demonstrate meeting the compliance requirements of the engagement with professional practice

Demonstrate professional conduct and communication skills, and the ability to work both autonomously and within a team, adapting to leadership roles as necessary and contributing effectively to team dynamics
Analyse and articulate the broad range of competencies required of a engineering associate, encompassing both technical and professional skills

Analyse and discuss the roles and responsibilities of engineers and managers within an organisation, including the structure, purpose, and operations of an engineering enterprise. and how engineers interact with internal and external stakeholders

Reflect on the influence of organisational culture on workplace functionality, considering aspects such as ethics, diversity, inclusivity and the integration of First Nations considerations, alongside the impact of the external environment on the performance of an engineering enterprise

Critically review professional conduct, reflect on professional development and the development of Engineers Australia Stage 1 Competencies at the engineering associatelevel, and assess ethical behaviours and decision-making in engineering practices

title: Leading Self and Others
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop an understanding of the theory of personal leadership and its relationship to leading others. Students evaluate the impact of personal leadership in a diversity of contexts and explore the influence of this on the capacity to lead others.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply the theoretical basis of self-leadership
Analyse and evaluate the impact of leader identity and self-leadership in educational contexts
Analyse and evaluate the impact of leader identity and self-leadership on leading others
Create a personal vision as a transformational leader of self and others
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7066 Leading Self and Others at the University of Adelaide

title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods
syllabus_overview: This course provides an introduction to the use of quantitative methods in research. Emphasis will be on achieving an understanding of quantitative methods and associated statistical techniques considered so that you can think critically about suitable procedures for research design, collection and analysis of data, and the usefulness of statistics. Students will gain experience with using the SPSS package on computers.
prerequisites: must have completed EDUC6022 Research Design
incompatibilities: must not have completed EDUC7011 Introduction to Quantitative Methods at the University of Adelaide

title: Environment I
syllabus_overview: The course explores the notion that designers respond to pressing environmental, cultural, social and economic issues in the design and creation of our built environments. The course introduces the historical, political and ethical contexts and processes of environmental design. The relationship between climates, environments and design as both built structures and landscapes is explored at a variety of scales. This course introduces students to the complex built environment and engineering contexts for the development of projects destined to shape our inevitably changing built environments.
learning_outcomes: Environment I introduces the relationship between specific environmental contexts (with emphasis on the bio-physical context) and design. The course provides the foundation for subsequent courses in the environment stream of the Bachelor of Architectural Design. The course learning outcomes for Environment I are specifically aligned with the thematic content of the lecture series, the tutorials, the required and recommended readings, the objectives of the assessable tasks, and importantly, the program learning outcomes. . analyse key aspects of the historical, political and ethical context of sustainable development, as well as Indigenous perspectives about the environment.
Identify the environmental, social and economic dimensions of sustainability.
Demonstrate understanding of sustainable processes, relating especially to biodiversity and water.
Employ the basic principles of sustainable design in a small project, including the selection of a plant palette.
Apply independent research skills to analyse and evaluate the relationship between climates, environments, and design.
Write clear and concise analytical texts which structure evidence for and against (a point of view) relating specifically to sustainable design.
incompatibilities: must not have completed DESST1508 Environment I at the University of Adelaide

title: Teaching and Learning in English Medium Instruction
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with advanced knowledge and professional skills to become leaders in the area of English medium instruction across diverse educational contexts.
learning_outcomes: Describe the foundations of EMI – its features, contextual variations and theoretical frameworks – and use this knowledge to analyse a specific EMI setting of choice, as a basis for potential pedagogical response

Investigate the nature of academic and disciplinary literacy and the linguistic dimensions of learning content through English in a particular discipline, to enable development of relevant support strategies and resources for teaching and learning
Apply distinctive features of EMI teaching and learning expertise to design a teaching unit, using evidence-based approaches to achieve effective pedagogical and assessment strategies

Develop and implement procedures and criteria for the effective management and delivery of EMI courses and programs, including professional development involving intercultural, linguistic and pedagogic competences

title: Families, Communities and Societal Wellbeing
syllabus_overview: Drawing on research from education, psychology, organisational psychology and the social sciences, this course explores issues of safety and wellbeing for individuals, families and communities, including the impacts of trauma and supporting recovery and fostering resilience.
learning_outcomes: Identify social processes impacting children, young people and their families
Understand and critically examine changing family contexts and impacts on children and young people
Identify and explain aspects of child safety, protection and abuse and respond effectively to assist children and young people while maintaining safe, inclusive learning and living environments
Understand and critically apply evidence-based approaches to support children and young people, their families and communities

title: Aircraft Design
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: In this course you will learn about Aircraft design methodology, Technical task preparation, team working, Aircraft design organisation, Aircraft weight calculation, mission fuel weight, Sensitivity analysis, Standard requirements, First estimation of aircraft design parameters, Sizing, Drag polar estimation at low speed, Matching diagram, Aircraft three view and drawings, Overall configuration design, Fuselage design, Propulsion system selection and integration, Wing design considerations, Empennage design considerations, Landing gear design and integration, Weight and balance analysis, Stability and control analysis. The material is presented in a combination of lectures, tutorials, hands-on laboratory sessions, and a group design project.
learning_outcomes: Complete conceptual design of different types of aircraft;
Discuss performance and stability analysis of different types of aircraft;
Explain the hierarchical models in aircraft design as a multi-disciplinary design objective and utilise a system approach to design and operational performance;
Discuss the design phases of an aircraft;
Explain the method of preparation design tasks and technical reports;
Calculate total weight and weight fractures of an aircraft;
Evaluate sensitivity analysis of design parameters;
Perform and understand sizing of an aircraft;

title: UO Project Management for Engineers
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The course aims to develop students' engineering application abilities and professional and personal attributes as defined by Engineers Australia. Particularly, it introduces students to relevant concepts, principles and techniques for effective leadership and management of engineering projects. Students will work in multidisciplinary teams to demonstrate the application of the socio-cultural, ethical and sustainable frameworks related to engineering projects. Activities will help students develop an understanding of the issues when working on multidisciplinary projects and expose them to a range of tools and techniques required in their discipline. Students will work on projects that will develop their communication, project management, teamwork and critical thinking skills.
learning_outcomes: Compare and distinguish between the specialisations within civil, mechanical and electrical engineering and demonstrate an understanding of the issues when working on a multidisciplinary project.
Identify appropriate tools and techniques to analyse and manage risks, and communicate engineering project plans that are relevant to the specialisation.
Demonstrate the application of the socio-cultural, ethical and sustainable frameworks related to engineering projects.
Apply and undertake project planning, monitoring and evaluation using modern tools and techniques for effective engineering project management.
Develop and apply professional reflection, critical thinking, referencing, teamwork, oral, written and visual communication skills appropriate for engineering practice.
incompatibilities: must not have completed ENGG2005 UO Project Management for Engineers at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed ENGG2004 Project Management for Engineers at the University of South Australia

title: UO Design Management for Engineers
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The course aims to develop students' engineering application abilities and professional and personal attributes as defined by Engineers Australia. The course will develop students' understanding of professional engineering practice and how this intersects with essential design management practices in diverse environments. The content is designed to extend students' technical competencies to the non-technical areas of engineering design. The activities will improve students' knowledge of contextual factors (economic, social, cultural, ethical, legal and environmental) and the impact these factors have on engineering projects. Students will work on projects that will develop their problem solving, communication, teamwork, leadership and critical thinking skills.
learning_outcomes: Apply standard systems engineering design concepts and methods (including system lifecycles, key systems design stages and activities, and supporting concepts including MBSE, ILS, TLS and sustainment) to the successful execution of a design project to a professional standard. Apply risk and opportunity concepts and assessments to engineering design projects.
Demonstrate a pro-active demeanour, professional and ethical conduct, and professional management and use of information in an engineering context.
Explain the non-technical aspects of design projects, including creativity and innovation, sustainability, safety and intellectual property protection.
Demonstrate professional reflection, critical thinking, research, teamwork, leadership, and oral, written and visual communication skills appropriate for engineering practice.
incompatibilities: must not have completed ENGG3007 UO Design Management for Engineers at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed ENGG3006 Design Management for Engineers at the University of South Australia

title: UO Engineering Design and Innovation
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course provides opportunities for students to build and extend a range of personal and professional skills. They will solve practical engineering design problems and recognise the roles of systems thinking, innovation and creativity in the design process. This course will help students to develop visual communication skills such as understanding and producing 2D engineering drawings and 3D engineering models. Course resources will introduce students to the exciting and complex world of engineering design and innovation. Activities and projects will help students to explore engineering problem solving, basic systems engineering concepts, creativity tools, engineering design process, project management principles, professional reflections, principles of safe design, link between ethics and creativity, and developing oral, written, and visual communication skills. This course will develop 2D and 3D visualisation skills and engineering drawing skills, which are essential to communicate designs while meeting industry drawing standards.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the civil, electrical, and mechanical engineering design process and the Australian Standard for technical drawing AS1100.
Develop visualisation and drawing skills and construct 2D drawings and 3D solid models to communicate design.
Work constructively and effectively as an individual and apply project management principles to solve practical engineering problems.
Apply the engineering design process, safe design principles and use innovation and creativity tools and techniques to develop an engineering solution.
Demonstrate developing professional reflection, oral, written and visual communication skills appropriate for engineering practice.
incompatibilities: must not have completed ENGG1005 UO Engineering Design and Innovation at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed ENGG1004 Engineering Design and Innovation at the University of South Australia

assessment_tasks.task_name: Concept Design, Design Project, Creative Work
Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions

title: Teaching and Learning Languages
syllabus_overview: This course introduces pedagogies and knowledges of languages learning for all languages courses.
learning_outcomes: Understand languages as a theorised field of education for diverse learners and learning contexts
Critically engage with languages curricula for diverse learners
Utilise contemporary perspectives in planning to teach and assess languages learning

title: Catholic Schools: Identity, Mission and Practice
syllabus_overview: To explore why Catholic Schools exist today, key research and beliefs about learners and teachers in Catholic Schools as well as pedagogies and professional practices that enhance the aims of Catholic Education. Participants will reflect on how Catholic theology contributes to the educator’s beliefs about children, childhood and adolescence, to their personal and professional identity and to choices about educational principles, methods and approaches best aligned to enhancing the mission of contemporary Catholic Schools.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically discuss how Catholic anthropology and Catholic Social Teaching Principles directly shape educational practices in Catholic Schools
Critically reflect on personal and professional teacher identity in the light of Catholic beliefs and values
Examine and critique approaches to teaching and learning in Catholic School classrooms to enhance contemporary understandings of identity and mission of Catholic Schools
Research, create, implement and evaluate a range of transformative practices appropriate for enhancing a contemporary Catholic School’s identity and mission
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUCX203 Catholic Scriptures: An Introduction/EDUCX204 Catholic Theology: An Introduction
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC2063 Contemporary Catholic Schools at the University of South Australia

title: Education Leadership in Diverse Contexts
syllabus_overview: This course will develop students’ understanding of contemporary issues in education leadership in diverse global contexts. These factors contribute to educational policy and practices and the changing role of leadership in educational contexts. Students will evaluate leadership models and strategies and their impact on teacher and student capacity, as well as develop skills to effectively lead and manage within diverse contexts, locally and internationally.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the complexities of educational leadership in diverse contexts.
Demonstrate an understanding of factors that contribute to educational policy and practices.
Demonstrate knowledge of the complexities and challenges of educational leadership.
Evaluate models and strategies of educational leadership and their impact on teacher and student capabilities.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7013 Educational Leadership in Diverse Contexts at the University of Adelaide

title: Arts for Secondary Teaching 2
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is for pre-service teachers to engage with relevant contemporary theory, practices, and curricula for Arts education in secondary schooling, including reference to a range of approaches to address diversity and inclusion. Learning in this course is sequential and scaffolded, building from Arts for Secondary Teaching 1. The course also includes a focus on Drama-Based Pedagogy (DBP) and Creative Body-Based Learning (CBL) teaching strategies.
learning_outcomes: Curate a range of arts and education resources appropriate for an inclusive pedagogical practice
Create a unit of work to demonstrate practical and theoretical understanding of inclusive practice, as well as a range of teaching strategies and strategies for differentiation and inclusion
Analyse and evaluate their planning in relation to themes of diversity and inclusive practices
Plan for and implement effective teaching and learning including a range of diverse teaching strategies
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUCX103 Effective Pedagogical Practices/EDUCX232 Arts for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Early Childhood Education: Contexts, History, Philosophy, Frameworks
syllabus_overview: This course aims to introduce the range of contexts of Early Childhood Education settings; history and philosophies of Early Childhood Education including contemporary and alternative perspectives and approaches to pedagogy and interactions; and begins exploration and development of knowledge of the frameworks that guide Early Childhood Education in Australia.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the discipline of early childhood education and knowledge of key policies and frameworks that shape contemporary early childhood education thinking and practices
Describe and critique theoretical and philosophical underpinnings of contemporary Australian early childhood education, including curriculum, policy and pedagogies
Reflect on the role of an early childhood educator, contemporary theories and pedagogies, and responsibility for ethical and culturally responsive practice

title: Engineering Materials
syllabus_overview: This course will provide students with knowledge of the relationship between the microstructure, properties, and processing of engineering materials. Students will be introduced to various families of engineering materials and their distinctive characteristics, enabling informed materials selection for specific engineering applications. The course will also cover key topics such as manufacturing processes, material degradation, and the environmental implications of material selection.
learning_outcomes: Explain the relationship between microstructure, processing, and material properties for a broad range of engineering materials
Analyse and interpret basic engineering data and measurements in relation to properties of engineering materials
Make appropriate materials selection to address basic engineering design challenges
Apply the life cycle analysis to make cost-effective, environmentally responsible materials selection in the context of engineering applications

assessment_tasks.task_name: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions

title: UO Sustainable Engineering Practice
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the engineering profession through course and project work and interaction with industry. All are designed to help students to develop some of the essential personal and professional skills needed for sustainable professional practice. Course resources will introduce students to a variety of areas in sustainable and professional engineering, including the role of the professional engineer, graduate attributes of engineering professionals, career management skills, critical analysis and reflective practice, principles of sustainable engineering, professional ethics, intercultural issues including Indigenous protocols, basic project management principles, effective teamwork, team roles, evaluation of team performance, engineering report writing, effective presentations, locating and using information and referencing.
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of the civil, electrical, and mechanical engineer in modern society.
Reflect on and demonstrate self-awareness of strengths and weaknesses relative to the attributes of professional engineers.
Demonstrate an awareness of the socio-cultural, safety, ethical, global and sustainable contexts in which engineering is practised.
Develop a solution to an engineering problem using inclusive teamwork skills and applying basic project management principles.
Demonstrate professional oral, written and visual communication skills appropriate for engineering practice.
incompatibilities: must not have completed ENGG1007 UO Sustainable Engineering Practice at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed ENGG1003 Sustainable Engineering Practice at the University of South Australia

title: Professional Experience 2: Inquiry into Practice
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to support preservice teachers to be successful in the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA) and the final placement in their program. Preservice teachers will draw on knowledge and skills from across their program as they engage in cycles of planning, teaching, assessing, reflecting and appraising growth in learning. These cycles will inform preservice teachers’ inquiries into practice during placement and the completion of the GTPA. On placement, preservice teachers will undertake the teaching load of a graduate teacher and demonstrate that they are performing at the graduate level of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.
learning_outcomes: Collect, interpret and use a range of data when planning for teaching and learning and when making adjustments to teaching and assessment practices
Apply the official curriculum, other resources and knowledge of prior learning to design connected teaching and learning sequences and effective assessments
Differentiate planning and teaching to meet the needs of all learners
Critically analyse and evaluate pedagogical and assessment decisions, and the progress of student learning, with reference to literature and theory
Maintain a safe and inclusive learning environment over a sustained time
prerequisites: must have completed EDUC6902 Professional Experience 1: Planning, Teaching, Assessing and Managing the Classroom Environment

title: Atmosphere and the Climate
syllabus_overview: To develop students’ awareness of the Earth’s weather systems and climate change, their skills in investigating, analysing and reporting, and their dispositions towards ecological sustainability, with a particular focus on the Earth’s atmosphere. Students will develop knowledge of the nature and operation of weather and climate systems, and issues around human impact on them. Ecological and carbon footprints, weather data gathering and reporting, integrally informed futures-oriented scenarios and climate change will be explored. This course will assist students develop their skills in investigating, analysing and reporting scientific data, and challenge their attitudes towards ecological sustainability, with respect to carbon footprint, weather parameters and climate change.
learning_outcomes: Describe major components and circulation patterns of the Earth's atmosphere, with a focus on the Southern Hemisphere
Demonstrate sound understandings of the history of, and human interactions with, the Earth's atmosphere and the implications of these for humans and other species
Use the techniques of integral Futures Studies to explore possibilities for future atmospheric management
Work individually and collaboratively to report on data collected from the literature and from field experiences
Communicate the value of individual and collective action to mitigate against deleterious effects of human interactions with the Earth's atmosphere and other natural systems

title: Early Numeracy
syllabus_overview: To develop students’ understanding of the relationship between Numeracy and early mathematical ideas, how children from birth to 5 years’ experience and construct numeracy in everyday contexts.
learning_outcomes: Identify young children’s (babies – toddlers - preschoolers) multi-modal communication of their mathematical understandings
Examine and identify young children’s intuitive construction of mathematical understanding and processes during numeracy experiences
Identify child-centered, play-based approaches appropriate for enhancing very young children’s mathematical understandings
Apply planning and evaluation strategies according to the EYLF planning cycle

title: Islamic Education: Critical Perspectives on Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
syllabus_overview: To re-examine the purpose and aspirations of Islamic schooling in relation to the 3 message systems of curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment. Drawing on Islamic Pedagogy, students enact an action research project relevant and urgent to their school context.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the contested nature of curriculum, pedagogy and assessment
Critically analyse diverse curriculum models, pedagogical approaches, and assessment methods employed in Islamic schools in relation to distinct visions, perspectives, and aims
Apply Islamic Pedagogy in the redesign of curriculum programming for purpose, coherence, and alignment
Reflexively consolidate the journey across the program and critically reflect on implications for renewal of Islamic schools

title: Understanding Complexities Impacting Families and Communities
syllabus_overview: This course will focus on the philosophical and evidence-informed approaches to wellbeing in families, society, and communities and how to advance society's prosperity, wellbeing and cohesion by addressing inequality and trauma in culturally diverse communities. The course explores how to cultivate wellbeing and explore differences between cultural factors, drawing on research from education, psychology, organisational psychology and the social sciences. Students will learn about philosophical approaches to wellbeing and systems-level and community perspectives that contribute to societal wellbeing, resilience and cohesion.
learning_outcomes: Identify social processes impacting children, young people and their families
Understand and critically examine changing family contexts and impacts on children and young people
Identify and explain aspects of child safety, protection and abuse and respond effectively to assist children and young people while maintaining safe, inclusive learning and living environments
Understand and critically apply evidence-based approaches to support children and young people, their families and communities

title: Production, Presentation and Audience in Arts Education
syllabus_overview: Preservice teachers will undertake practice-led arts workshops focusing on creative processes and pedagogical content leading to a presentation. Reflective documentation will include application to diverse learning contexts with connections to other key learning areas. Approaches to production include critical thinking with pedagogical strategies for inclusion and design thinking. SUGGESTED CHANGE: This course aims to equip pre-service teachers for their future role as an educational leader for children's arts learning, applying knowledge of arts practices and approaches in arts education and undertaking professional engagement with a site to design and implement an arts project.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the role and function of the arts as a means of communication for young people in diverse contemporary communities
Identify and research traditional and contemporary approaches to production, presentation and audiences within arts curricula
Research and develop arts creative processes and practices to produce and present performance, presentation or display for an audience
Critically analyse current approaches to technologies for working in the arts in relation to production, presentation and audience
Identify cultural knowledge and influences intrinsic to the development and creation of art works
Critically reflect on practice as an active arts educator

title: Advanced Islamic Civilisation
syllabus_overview: To provide students with an advanced knowledge of the history of the Islamic civilisation from the time of prophet Muhammad to the fall of the Ottoman Empire. In doing so the course will examine the social, political and religious factors that led to the formation of a formidable Islamic civilisation that continues to influence the modern world.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the evolving nature of the Islamic civilisation and its impact on contemporary Muslim societies
Evaluate the causes that led to the rise and fall of various Islamic empires
Examine the social, political and religious contexts of various Islamic empires in different geographical regions
Present a case that highlights the relations, commonalities and differences between the Islamic and Western Civilisations
incompatibilities: must not have completed EDUC5276 Advanced Islamic Civilisation at the University of South Australia

title: Learning About Text Production and Writing Genres
syllabus_overview: This course develops students English teaching skills in the areas of multimodal text production and genres. Students will develop knowledge of text production from a semiotic perspective, inclusive of linguistic and non-linguistic modalities and a range of production technologies. Students will focus on producing texts in a range of genres, including narrative, informational and persuasive genres, using a variety of modes. Students will learn pedagogies for teaching writing and multi-modal text production in diverse classroom contexts, building on knowledge of literacy, language and literature gained in previous English courses. Students will learn to use quality literature and writing processes to support learning about literary and imaginative writing.
learning_outcomes: Describe and critically analyse theoretical perspectives that inform contemporary English teaching in and spoken, written and multimodal text production
Apply genre theory to the design and production of multimodal texts
Apply detailed knowledge of the language and literary features and patterns of texts to interpret and create texts
Design and justify planning and assessment approaches to inform teaching and learning for writing and text production
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding different theoretical perspectives of learner difference and the implications for inclusive teaching of English
Apply, justify and demonstrate a range of strategies for designing teaching learning programs for writing and text production

title: Group Dynamics for Education
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip learners with the necessary knowledge and skills to enhance their ability to operate effectively within groups and to plan to facilitate the learning of social skills as future educators in Primary school settings. This psychosocial course draws on foundations in group dynamics and positive psychology to explore the complexities of effective group functioning and to understand human behaviour. There is a focus on personal responsibility and the application of key ideas to social and emotional development in primary education. The course places a strong emphasis on the process of reflective evaluation and transformation to build team effectiveness and promote personal development. Experiential learning tasks connect and integrate theory and practice throughout the course, and they provide a range of opportunities to develop skills in collaboration, communication and leadership capacities to influence group functioning.
learning_outcomes: Develop your knowledge of the complexities of effective group functioning and explore how human behaviour plays a significant role in shaping this dynamic
Evaluate the development of the functioning capacity of an operating (GAIT) group
Facilitate a Group Adventure Initiative Task and the reflective debrief to appraise the group’s functioning
Investigate educational resources for enhancing social and emotional development for Primary children and report on how one program could be applied to a primary educational context

title: Learning About Literacies and Literatures
syllabus_overview: This course aims to introduce and examine early literacy theories, practices and multimodal literature for children of diverse backgrounds and experiences, including in English, multicultural and multilingual contexts.
learning_outcomes: Understand and critically appraise different theories, models, and practices for literacy learning
Apply understandings of multimodality and plurilingualism to the models and practices for literacy learning
Explain the role of imagination and literary texts in children’s development and learning
Identify and critically analyse quality literature and authentic texts from a range of historical, social, and cultural contexts
Apply detailed knowledge of a range of literary theories and the language and literary features and patterns to the analysis of literary, non-fiction and multimodal texts
Apply strategies for responding to literary texts to planning for teaching and learning

title: Accounting Curriculum and Pedagogy
syllabus_overview: The focus of this course and its companion Curriculum and Pedagogy is learning and teaching theory and its application in practice for teaching. This includes planning, developing and assessing learning for diverse student cohorts in line with the Australian and SACE Curriculum requirements in this subject specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate deep knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance, and structure of the content area and the complexity of the discipline teaching strategies in the learning area.
Design and sequence unit and lesson plans based on essential content of the subject area, curriculum and assessment principles.
Demonstrate understanding of assessment, moderation, and its application to support consistent and comparable judgments of student learning, and so as to modify teaching practices.
Integrate relevant research and theory to develop a broad repertoire of subject-appropriate teaching and learning strategies, including the use of ICT.
incompatibilities: must not have completed EDUC7105 Accounting Curriculum and Pedagogy at the University of Adelaide

title: English for Secondary Teaching 2
syllabus_overview: This course prepares students to understand developmental stages in learning to read and to teach reading in the early years settings, utilising a range of methods and approaches including phonics-based learning and meaning making strategies, incorporating multimodalities and catering to diverse learner groups with a range of language backgrounds.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate broad and coherent content knowledge for the teaching of English and literature
Demonstrate knowledge of planning for socially and culturally inclusive and relevant teaching in English with reference to Australian Curriculum, SACE and/or IB Programs
Plan developmentally appropriate sequences of learning and assessment with an explicit focus on the senior secondary years
Critically reflect on the social and cultural impact of literature and texts in subject English
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUCX103 Effective Pedagogical Practices/EDUCX419 English for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Antennas and Propagation
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: To develop the knowledge and skills of the fundamental principles of antennas, propagation of electromagnetic waves, applications, design, analysis and testing, beam scanning/forming and array design for advanced wireless systems.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the important elements of antenna and propagation theory
Calculate and apply fundamental antenna parameters
Compare important classes of antennas and their properties
Select a particular class of antenna for given specifications
Apply theoretical principles to design an antenna, using EM simulation tools
Explain techniques for estimating the propagation performance of a communication channel
Define specifications for a communications system based on a set of requirements
prerequisites: must have completed ENGE3001 Electromagnetic Engineering

assessment_tasks.task_name: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration

title: Arts Education
syllabus_overview: This course introduces interdisciplinary pedagogies and content knowledge for the Arts Education learning areas: Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music, and Visual Arts.
learning_outcomes: Employ knowledge of Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and Visual Arts in the Arts curriculum
Document and plan authentic Arts learning experiences, using a range of resources including technologies

Apply an understanding of the cultural diversity within classrooms and communities in Australia, and in the local context, to understand and value the perspectives of diverse groups including EAL/D and First Nations students
Apply an understanding of the contribution of The Arts to learners' wellbeing
Understand the concept of ongoing intercultural development and the importance of self-reflection and reflexivity as ever-evolving career practices

assessment_tasks.task_name: Peer Review, Portfolio, Multiple Choice Questions
Skills Demonstration, Assessment Plan, Critical Analysis

title: Telecommunication Device and Network Security
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide foundational training in methods of hardware-based security for securing telecommunication devices and methods of network security for securing telecommunication networks.
learning_outcomes: Identify common hardware-level vulnerabilities, attacks, and defences applicable to telecommunication devices.
Identify common vulnerabilities, attacks and defences at different layers of a network protocol stack.
Compare and contrast different intrusion detection methods and use an intrusion detection tool.
Implement cryptographic protocols using established cryptographic libraries.
Simulate discrete-variable quantum key distribution.

Discuss Diffie-Hellman key exchange, Transport Layer Security (TLS), post-quantum cryptography and discrete-variable quantum key distribution in terms of their principles and their roles in securing end-to-end communications.
prerequisites: Must have completedENGEX421Telecommunication System Security

assessment_tasks.task_name: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task

title: Teaching and Learning Motor Skills
syllabus_overview: In this course students will explore fundamental movement skills to craft and organise appropriate learning experiences for diverse learners in primary settings, unpacking the pedagogical implications. Planning will aim to foster success, inclusivity, and participation within a supportive learning environment. The play practice approach to teaching is explored to develop novice learners across a variety of games and sports.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and document individual diversity in movement capabilities and characteristics associated with the spectrum of novice learners
Devise and structure aligned learning situations which are inclusive and promote maximum individual participation
Explore fundamental movement skills and their application in appropriate learning experiences for junior primary students
Evaluate theory and demonstrate the ability to apply simplifying, shaping, and enhancing processes using Play Practice principles
Plan and teach a series of sequenced lessons to develop the novice learner across various categories of games and sports

title: Thinking and Working Mathematically
syllabus_overview: The aim of the course is for pre-service teachers to learn and apply strategies for thinking and working mathematically in the primary years of schooling, both for themselves and in planning for learning. The course draws on and extends the proficiency and process strands of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics.
learning_outcomes: Select, apply, and evaluate mathematical problem-solving strategies for solving unfamiliar problems, including a focus on algebraic reasoning
Plan developmentally appropriate sequences of learning with an explicit focus on thinking and working mathematically
Interpret and use student work to plan for student-centred lessons with a focus on thinking and working mathematically
prerequisites: must have completed all of EDUC2011 Developing Number Sense/EDUCX221 Reasoning with Statistics and Probability/EDUCX223 Spatial Reasoning

assessment_tasks.task_name: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration

title: Children's Growth and Development
syllabus_overview: This course aims to deepen knowledge about children's growth and development from conception to adolescence and examine research on ways to use this knowledge to support children's learning, development and wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Describe sequences of development in children and use these to plan support for children
Identify and communicate the importance of environmental influences on development
Assess child development using objective observations and science-based knowledge
Plan to support children’s development
incompatibilities: Must not have completedEDUC1041Children's Development Conception to 3 Years at the University of South Australia

title: Teaching Linguistically Diverse Learners
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip students with theoretical understandings and pedagogical strategies needed to teach learners of English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EALD). Students will enhance their understanding of EALD learners and their learning in mainstream classes; develop pedagogical strategies and assessments; and create resources to support EALD students to access and engage with learning areas across the curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the linguistic, cultural and learning needs of linguistically diverse learners
Analyse the linguistic demands of their teaching context
Critically investigate an approach to teaching linguistically diverse learners in the context of language acquisition research
Evaluate and justify the selection of a range of strategies for making learning accessible to linguistically diverse learners

title: Becoming an Educator with an Arts Specialisation
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop deep understanding of traditional, contemporary and emerging arts content and practices, their application to the curriculum and the role/s of a generalist primary school teacher with an arts curriculum specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role and function of the arts in diverse contemporary communities and their impact upon young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to the arts in curriculum decision making and research
Experience creative body-based learning in physical, digital and virtual spaces
Apply current approaches to technology in working with digital and media arts
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts as intrinsic to Australian histories and cultural knowledge
Articulate the intrinsic and instrumental value of visual arts, media arts, dance, drama and music in the school curriculum
Demonstrate reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator with young people

title: Curriculum Connections
syllabus_overview: To develop conceptual and foundational content knowledge in HASS: Civics and Citizenship and HASS: Economics and Business, examining contemporary issues and connections across all four HASS substrands. Pre-service teachers will apply personal and global lenses to explore how these disciplines connect to History and Geography within the Australian Curriculum Foundation to Year 6.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the connections between HASS: Civics and Citizenship and HASS: Economics and Business with History and Geography
Apply pedagogical content knowledge to the teaching of HASS: Civics and Citizenship and HASS: Economics and Business, including out-of-school activities.
Integrate Civics and Citizenship and Economics and Business into the teaching of History and Geography through content knowledge, concepts, skills, and achievement standards

title: Information Theory and Coding
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: To introduce the basic tools and concepts in information theory, and practical coding schemes for data compression and transmission over noisy channels.
learning_outcomes: Examine mathematically the notion of information contained in data and the fundamental limits to compress data for efficient storage
Analyse and compare the roles of redundancy in combating the effect of noise in various communications media
Develop the connections between information-theoretic schemes and algebraic/convolutional/graph-based schemes for communicating data over discrete memoryless channels
Examine and derive the operations involved in different encoders and decoders, and be able to compare the advantages and disadvantages of various coding paradigms
Examine and evaluate advanced literature in the field of information theory and coding
Use problem-solving and computing skills to analyse and derive efficient means of representation, storage and transmission of information in communications networks

title: Languages and Language in Use
syllabus_overview: This course considers concepts of language and languages, including systems of language and the social and cultural contexts in which languages are developed and used. Students will be introduced to theories of language to develop their understanding of languages as meaning-making systems through which the world is shaped and interpreted. Students will explore language variation through the concepts of plurilingualism and translanguaging, and key social variables such as gender, age, and social class. They will explore language use through global, national and local perspectives to understand language diversity in all communities, and to reflect on their own language identities and knowledges.
learning_outcomes: Understand how language(s) change across time and space based on a range of socio-cultural circumstances
Demonstrate how language-and-culture are integrally related
Critically analyse how conceptualisations of language-and-culture are informed by a variety of theoretical positions
Distinguish elements of language and how they vary across languages

title: Food Technology 1
syllabus_overview: This course aims to introduce preservice teachers to the skills, knowledge and professional expertise associated with teaching and learning in design and technologies food specialisms, in both primary and middle school settings, with a strong focus on integrating both the theoretical and practical aspects of food technologies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the latest technologies and design principles in planning and developing relevant and engaging food technology lessons in line with the Australian Curriculum
Identify the societal influences on food production and food choices
Exhibit and critically analyse food preparation and production techniques when designing solutions suitable for primary and middle school classrooms
Apply WHS knowledge in identifying and applying food safety and hygiene practices, as well as safe use of tools and equipment in the food technology classroom

title: Drama and Visual Arts: Story Landscapes
syllabus_overview: This course will deepen and extend students' traditional, contemporary drama and visual arts subject knowledge for work in school settings.
learning_outcomes: Employ an understanding of the role and function of Drama and Visual Arts in diverse contemporary communities and their impact upon young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to Drama and Visual Arts in curriculum decision making and research
Apply current and appropriate pedagogies for working with Drama and Visual Arts
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander storytelling and visual arts as intrinsic to Australian cultural knowledge, understanding and communication
Articulate the intrinsic and instrumental value of Drama, and Visual Arts in the school curriculum
Employ reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator

title: Design and Production 1
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce and develop an understanding of the use of computer aided design (CAD) software packages to visualise and design solutions in order to produce designs into a physical project through the use of laser cutting, 3D printing or CNC machining. Pre-service teachers will develop their expertise in operating state of the art machinery and maintaining best workshop practices. Additionally, students are introduced to sustainability in design and production processes while ensuring all practices meet WHS requirements.
learning_outcomes: Apply a design process to research, design and develop innovative products using sustainable materials, processes, technologies and systems
Identify the specific characteristics, properties and appropriate usage of various types of materials and composite materials
Apply WHS knowledge to competently and safely operate a range of state-of-the-art digital equipment as well as hand and power tools and machines to realise products in tangible materials
Apply critical thinking in evaluating products in terms of design, materials and systems production

title: Learning About Language
syllabus_overview: The course aims to develop students understanding of theories of language, including developmental theory, sociocultural theory, semiotic theory and systemic functional linguistics.
learning_outcomes: Explain the connections between language, culture, identity and home and community languages
Understand and explain the implications of culturally sustaining and expanding pedagogies to support and value plurilingualism and variation in language learning
Explain that language learning, language development and language practices are influenced by sociocultural contexts, through a functional model of language
Analyse and apply the levels of language (sounds, words, grammar and sentences, register and genre) to texts in various modes to inform teaching
Apply a functional theory of language development and its implications for educational settings

title: Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara Language and Culture 2
syllabus_overview: This course aims to extend students’ basic understandings of Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara language and culture, including pronunciation, grammar, and the cultural context of Anangu communities. Students will develop an increasing understanding of building complexity and meaning in Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara language use.
learning_outcomes: Extend language skills and understand increasingly complex grammar in Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara
Deepen understanding of the significance of Aboriginal languages in Australia and ethical use of and engagement with Aboriginal people and their languages
Work with Anangu to develop skills as translators and interpreters

title: Chinese Curriculum & Pedagogy
syllabus_overview: The focus of this course and its companion Curriculum and Pedagogy is learning and teaching theory and its application in practice for teaching. This includes planning, developing and assessing learning for diverse student cohorts in line with the Australian and SACE Curriculum requirements in this subject specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate deep knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance, and structure of the content area and the complexity of the discipline teaching strategies in the learning area.
Design and sequence unit and lesson plans based on essential content of the subject area, curriculum and assessment principles.
Demonstrate understanding of assessment, moderation, and its application to support consistent and comparable judgments of student learning, and so as to modify teaching practices.
Integrate relevant research and theory to develop a broad repertoire of subject-appropriate teaching and learning strategies, including the use of ICT.
incompatibilities: must not have completed EDUC7109 Chinese Curriculum & Pedagogy at the University of Adelaide

title: Mathematics Education 2
syllabus_overview: This course will examine the importance of developing children’s productive dispositions towards mathematics and how to develop children’s capacity for thinking and working mathematically. PSTs will examine current research in mathematics education and how it can be applied to inform their planning and practice. Throughout the course, PSTs will explore important pedagogical issues, including anticipating student responses, using multiple representations and differentiation. This course focuses on planning teaching and learning experiences of mathematics at a unit level that are informed by the curriculum framework and includes a focus on summative assessment.
learning_outcomes: Effectively plan, implement, and evaluate sequences of learning in mathematics that support the participation and learning of all children with a particular emphasis on the mathematical processes and proficiencies.
Demonstrate capacity to use data and evidence of children’s thinking to inform teacher practice.
Develop, select, and use a range of resources, including digital resources, for teaching and assessing children’s mathematical understanding.
Demonstrate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of numeracy, including the explicit teaching of mathematics and building fluency, understanding, problem-solving and reasoning

title: Learning English as an Additional Language
syllabus_overview: The course aims to equip pre-service teachers with the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively teach English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EALD). It explores the multifaceted nature of language and culture, their acquisition and use, and their implications for teaching and learning. Through both theoretical and practical approaches, the course fosters an understanding of multilingual pedagogies and culturally responsive practices. Additionally, it enhances students' abilities to design and implement lesson plans that cater to diverse linguistic backgrounds, while also developing critical thinking and reflective practices to create inclusive and effective learning environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and apply theories of additional language learning in EALD pedagogy.
Interpret and apply resources from the Australian Curriculum and other relevant frameworks to support EALD learners.
Develop and evaluate effective EALD lesson planning and assessment strategies.
Demonstrate effective teaching skills by applying EALD instructional strategies and integrating diverse, multimodal resources to support learners through micro-teaching.
Reflect critically on teaching practices, incorporating multilingual pedagogies and culturally responsive practices to create inclusive learning environments.
incompatibilities: Must not have completedEDUC5108Learning English as an Additional Language at the University of South Australia

title: Spatial Reasoning
syllabus_overview: The aim of the course is to develop the mathematical skills and knowledge for teaching mathematics in the primary years of schooling, with a focus on developing spatial reasoning through deep conceptual understanding of the curriculum content of measurement and geometry. This course will focus on developing subject-matter knowledge relevant for Primary mathematics, focusing on mathematical concepts, identifying relationships in and between these concepts and how these concepts progress and develop in the primary years. The course has a strong focus on using digital technologies effectively for teaching mathematics and draws on content from the Measurement and Space content strands of the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics.
learning_outcomes: Design and present a mathematical problem with a focus on measurement and geometry
Critique the role of digital technologies in measurement and geometry with a focus on conceptual and spatial reasoning, perspective, and visualisation
Demonstrate their capacity to communicate mathematically through the processes of problem solving, reasoning, verifying, reflecting and applying
prerequisites: must have completed EDUC2011 Developing Number Sense

title: Science for Secondary Teaching 2
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to build preservice teachers’ ability to apply and scrutinise a range of contemporary practices, including inquiry approaches, to engage, challenge and assess scientific understanding of all learners. They will critically analyse prevailing modes of teaching science and explore ways to enhance participation and engagement for all students. Preservice teachers will analyse how key curriculum documents, such as the Australian Curriculum and SACE, shape secondary school science teaching and learning, and empower their students to be scientifically literate and informed citizens.
learning_outcomes: Apply, analyse and evaluate a range of pedagogies, including inquiry-based approaches, that are used for teaching science in secondary schools
Design, enact and critically reflect on teaching and learning sequences that support the learning of all students
Develop, select and evaluate a range of assessments appropriate for secondary school science that support the learning of all students
Effectively plan science units of work that are appropriate for particular contexts and purposes
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUCX103 Effective Pedagogical Practices/EDUCX237 Science for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Growth, Health and Development
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to a developmental model of how young people grow and mature together and the inextricable relationship this has on the emergence of movement capabilities. The course focuses on the early childhood to adolescent stages of human growth and motor development and encourages a holistic view of development. The knowledge and skills acquired throughout the course will enhance capabilities to teach the whole child using movement as a valuable medium. A focus on planning and teaching social dance, fundamental athletics skills and general gymnastics in developmentally appropriate ways, to children in the Primary years of school will be explicitly modelled with the opportunity for students to enhance their own abilities.
learning_outcomes: Explain the characteristics and principles of human growth, development and motor behaviour from birth to adolescence in relation to the application into teaching practice

Understand and describe the complex process of change and critical periods in human development and motor behaviour that emerges from the interaction of heredity, task and the environment (Hourglass model)
Use key terms associated with the study of human growth and development appropriately to contribute to small group discussion and learning activities
Explain how the periods of life are inextricably linked with the phases of motor development through the Hourglass Model of motor development
Apply knowledge and understanding of human growth and motor development from birth to adolescence to plan developmentally appropriate and engaging learning sequences for primary-aged students
Demonstrate teaching skills in the developmentally appropriate activities for the early and primary years of schooling

title: Islamic Education: Principles and Praxis
syllabus_overview: To foster a deep epistemic reflexivity about the need for renewal in Islamic schools. This course centres meta-purpose for Islamic school settings and grounds students in Islamic Pedagogy as a distinct philosophy of education. To examine theories, principles and philosophies of Islamic education as they inform Islamic pedagogy and evaluate the implications for diverse approaches to quality teaching and learning for Muslim students in contemporary classrooms.
learning_outcomes: Explore and critically analyse the relationship between ontology and epistemology and conceptions of education
Critically compare and situate the meta purpose embedded within philosophies of Islamic education to contemporary approaches to Islamic schooling
Engage in epistemic reflexivity aligning what we believe about education with how we educate in Islamic school settings
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC5262 Islamic Pedagogy Principles and Praxis at the University of South Australia

title: Technology by Design
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop students knowledge, skills, and expertise in, design thinking, enterprise learning, entrepreneurship, STEM and technology-based pedagogies. Through engagement in project based learning and cross-discipline planning, students will apply their skills to meet the needs of a community, industry or organisation and connect their learning to practical STEM and entrepreneurial education practices.
learning_outcomes: Identify, plan and teach aspects of STEM and enterprise learning through a project-based inquiry approach
Apply the design-thinking process to develop critical and creative thinking, when solving complex problems
Select and use resources appropriate to design and technologies
Develop the capacity to work with colleagues to plan for, to evaluate and to improve teaching and learning through technology, entrepreneurial learning and design thinking education

title: Use of Technology in Humanities and Social Sciences
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop an appreciation of the range of technologies available and a capacity to effectively apply technology in the Humanities and Social Sciences classroom to engage and enhance learning outcomes for all students.
