title: Rights and Development
syllabus_overview: This course examines the relationship between human rights and international development with a focus on countries of the Global South. It introduces students to human rights as frameworks for social change and to rights-based approaches as tools of development policy and practice. Drawing on case studies from across the Global South, the course critically examines how human rights frameworks shape and are shaped by economic, social, and political development processes in contexts of poverty and inequality. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of both the strengths and limitations of rights-based approaches, equipping them to engage critically with contemporary debates in international development policy and practice.
learning_outcomes: Explain the theoretical and historical connections between human rights and development thinking and practice, including the evolution from needs-based to rights-based approaches.
Critically analyse human rights-based approaches (HRBAs) to development across economic, social, political, and human development domains.
Evaluate the role of key actors including states, international institutions, civil society, and affected communities in advancing or undermining rights in development practice.
Apply human rights frameworks to contemporary development challenges facing Global South countries, including poverty, inequality, climate vulnerability, and democratic governance.
Engage critically with debates around ethics, universalism, sovereignty, and power in the international human rights and development landscape

Collaborate effectively in team-based learning environments by contributing to group inquiry into rights and development issues and demonstrate critical self- and peer-assessment skills through reflective engagement with diverse perspectives.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Case Study, Case Study, Peer Review

title: Memory Wars: History and Society
syllabus_overview: This course aims to explore the relationship between history and its afterlives in the present through an examination of how public historical memory is made and remade in commemoration and memorial practices. Drawing upon case studies from western democracies around the world, the course aims to contextualise global discussions about how we reconcile with contested national histories.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the social, political and cultural conditions in which historical knowledge is produced and be able to connect this understanding to contemporary social debates
Identify and evaluate appropriate historical sources and apply historical evidence
Produce effective written argument and participate respectfully in team-based critical analysis and problem-solving

Demonstrate communication skills appropriate to career readiness, including use of online learning technologies, skills of collaborative and self-directed critical thinking, and sensitivity to the intercultural and ethical contexts of a diverse learning environment

title: Development Regulations and Building Codes
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop students’ understanding of planning and building regulations relevant to the construction industry. It covers the development approval process, as well as the key codes and standards that govern construction activities in Australia.
learning_outcomes: Relate the principles of development and control to various projects and localities
Review the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act and Regulations and the related Australian standards
Relate the Building Code of Australia to construction projects using drawings and other information
Compose reports on building and planning matters and analyse non-compliance with regulations
incompatibilities: Must not have completed BUIL4028

title: Materials Selection for Engineering Design
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: To introduce students to various tools that can be used to select the appropriate material and the fabrication route for production of a given engineering component. Examination of various failure modes to identify failure mechanism in real life examples. Apply the concept of material selection and knowledge acquired from failure analysis techniques to improve useful life of engineering parts and prevent their premature failure. Reviews of available materials, manufacturing processes and mechanical behaviour of materials including fracture, fatigue, creep, corrosion and wear are also included in this course to enable the implementation of materials selection. In addition, the energy consumption for materials production and fabrication are briefly discussed to enable the students to realize the effect of engineering parts production on the environment.
learning_outcomes: Rationalize and justify the selection of materials for engineering applications based on relevant properties, performance and economic criteria.
Evaluate available fabrication routes and justify the selection of appropriate route for a given material and application.
Appraise the environmental impact of selected materials and fabrication routes, including energy consumption and recyclability.
Analyze the causes and mechanisms of common failure modes in engineering parts
Apply knowledge of failure mechanisms to inform materials selection, process selection, and engineering design decisions.
Collaborate effectively in teams to plan, communicate, and make evidence-based decisions in materials engineering context.
prerequisites: must have completed all of ENGI1002 Engineering Materials/ENGM2008 Mechanics of Materials and Structures

title: Construction Management Research Dissertation A
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to locate and critically review literature related to an identified research topic; and consequently, develop a research proposal. Building upon fundamentals of scientific research, this course provides opportunities for students to practice in construction management specific paradigms. By designing a research proposal, students will develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills related to construction management related research. This course aligns with the program's intent to prepare future leaders of the construction industry that are able to locate and solve problems with proper research skills.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced understanding of principles of construction management related research
Locate, evaluate and critique existing studies related to selected research topic
Identify the gap within the existing body of knowledge and research questions
Demonstrate advanced understanding of common research paradigms, methods and tools for construction management
Develop a research proposal related to construction management
prerequisites: Must have completed BLDGX300 Construction Management Research Methods
incompatibilities: Must not have completedBLDG6003Construction Management Research Dissertation B at the University of Adelaide

title: Construction Economics and Procurement
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The course aims to equip students with knowledge relating to the fundamentals of micro-economic and macro-economic theory as well as procurement methods used for construction projects. Upon successful completion of the course, students will have a fundamental understanding of how the national economy and construction sector is affected by the global economy and the government’s approach to monetary and fiscal policies. Students will also have a comprehensive understanding of the various methods used in the construction industry to procure construction services including construct only, design & construct, cost plus, remeasurement, management contracting, construction management, public private partnerships and alliance contracting. Overall, the course will improve students’ critical thinking and interpreting skills along with communication skills. This course aligns with the program’s intent of providing knowledge to commence professional practice in construction management disciplines.
learning_outcomes: Describe the economic characteristics of the construction industry
Describe fundamental micro-economic theory and relate it to firms in the construction industry
Discuss fundamental macroeconomic theory explaining the behaviour of construction output and its relationship to national economic output

Identify the various stages of the traditional construction project lifecycle and explain the key activities that take place at each stage including the roles of the construction stakeholders/professionals involved
Describe the traditional and novel project procurement methods commonly used in the construction industry
Appraise the suitability of procurement methods commonly used in the construction industry for various types of construction projects
incompatibilities: Must not have completed BUIL 1023 Introduction to Construction Business Management at the University of South Australia

title: Human Behaviour and Conservation 3
school: School of Phys, Chem and E Sci
syllabus_overview: This course aims to enable students to critically explore human behaviour as it relates to conservation and barriers to environmentally responsibly behaviours.Using a psychological perspective, students will evaluate strategies to facilitate behaviour change in support of conservation of the natural environment.
learning_outcomes: Explain key psychological principles of advertising and persuasion, core principles of behaviour change, and ethical considerations relevant to their application in conservation and marketing contexts
Analyse contemporary marketing materials and conservation initiatives to determine how psychological principles are applied to influence human behaviours.
Interpret and evaluate behaviour data using appropriate measurement approaches and analytical concepts relevant to conservation behaviour change.

Critically evaluates current conservation research to identify a threat or problem relevant to the conservation of a species or environment that may be addressed through ethical human behaviour change.
Design a conservation strategy centred on a specific human behaviour that demonstrates understanding in persuasive communication, psychological principles, and community based social marketing
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of BIOL1032 Ecological Issues 1/ENVI2007 Environmental Interpretation and Community Engagement

title: Project Appraisal
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course will develop knowledge and skills to conduct a project appraisal to justify a recommendation to a client. Content includes: decision making and project appraisal; challenges of multi attributed decision-making; risk sensitivity; cash flow; time value of money; present worth evaluation; rate of return; estimating the benefit/cost ratio; identifying and quantifying non-financial benefits/externalities; strategic analysis; technical analysis; environmental analysis political analysis; social analysis post appraisal processes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the project appraisal process and an ability to critically evaluate projects using appraisal techniques.
Analyse a range of economic values and exercise judgment in applying these values in the context of real world problems.
Demonstrate professional communication skills to transmit knowledge and ideas to others in a manner which is clear and coherent.
Use critical thinking to synthesise data from multiple sources to identify and solve project appraisal problems with intellectual independence.
incompatibilities: must not have completed BUIL3025 UO Project Appraisal at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed BUIL3011 Project Appraisal at the University of South Australia

title: Commercial Management
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: To provide students with essential knowledge and skills in relation to the commercial management of finance, working capital, cash flow, project costs, time-related prolongation costs, variations to contract scope, payment and final accounts on construction projects.
learning_outcomes: Generate financial viability reports, cash flow forecasts, cost reports and model working capital requirements with respect to construction projects
Evaluate prolongation costs arising from project delays, as well as the management of price fluctuations and cost escalation in construction projects.

Prepare and calculate interim progress payment claims, payment certificates/schedules, and final accounts on construction projects according to contractual requirements. Demonstrate an understanding of how post-contract variations to the scope of works are directed and valued according to contractual requirements.

Explain and demonstrate how the statutory payment and adjudication schemes in the building and construction industry security of payment legislation affect progress and final payments on construction projects
prerequisites: must have completed BLDG4007 Construction Contract Administration

title: Infrastructure Construction
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to build an understanding of construction technology as applied to infrastructure projects including measurement and cost estimating of infrastructure work.
learning_outcomes: Understand the construction technologies applied to infrastructure projects
Understand the construction process of infrastructure projects
Propose cost plans of transport infrastructure projects based on measurement and estimating
Evaluate procurement methods and tendering strategies for infrastructure projects
prerequisites: must have completed all of ARCH1009 Construction Science and Materials/BLDG1002 Low-rise Construction and Land Surveying

title: Environmental Systems and Sustainability
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course provides an introductory overview to the topic of sustainability, and will help students develop the engineering competencies required to address the uncertain, complex and ambiguous nature of sustainability challenges.
learning_outcomes: Describe key characteristics of system thinking and apply system thinking methods to the diagnosis of environmental and sustainable development challenges
Describe and apply causal models to environmental accidents, and identify approaches that engineers can take to mitigate accidents and enhance the environmental safety of engineered systems
Summarise different types of environmental pollution, including physical, chemical, biological, acoustic and radiation, and identify engineering solutions to mitigate pollution
Articulate different approaches to community engagement, and the value of participation and respecting different cultural, value and knowledge systems in developing sustainable solutions
Demonstrate an understanding of the key steps in assessing the environmental impacts for a large engineering development
Articulate and explain the core competencies that engineers need to address the uncertain, ambiguous and complex nature of achieving sustainable solutions
incompatibilities: Must not have completed ENV ENG 1001

title: Integrated Learning
syllabus_overview: This advanced level course offers students the chance to engage in an industry experience, where they apply theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. Its goal is to improve students' professional competencies, interpersonal skills, business consulting abilities, and applied research skills. Additionally, the course emphasises the importance of promoting individual responsibility for professional growth and development.
learning_outcomes: Apply discipline-based business knowledge to a professional work environment
Communicate and interact effectively with work colleagues
Effectively use data generated by the business and from other sources
Perform tasks set by an employer to a satisfactory standard

Reflect on their experience in the work environment and how this relates to the enhancement of their professional competencies and the deepening and broadening of their business knowledge and ethical action
Demonstrate Business Enterprise Skills in Self-Management; Problem Solving, Ethical Awareness, Oral and Written Communication at advanced level

title: Field Geoscience Program 3
school: School of Phys, Chem and E Sci
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop the capability to interpret and convey geological relationships across multiple spatial and temporal scales via independent geological mapping. Students apply field observations, structural and stratigraphic principles, and geospatial data to investigate, identify and analyse rock units and their relationships. Students will also integrate their own field observations with published datasets to construct geological maps and develop models that effectively demonstrate and communicate the geological evolution of the study area. An emphasis is placed on extrapolating and synthesising evidence to reconstruct tectonic, depositional, and Earth system processes. The analytical and interpretative skills developed are transferable to a wide range of geological settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate professional and ethical conduct during geological fieldwork, working effectively and responsibly in team environments
Apply field-based methods to systematically identify, measure, and document geological features, including lithologies, structures, and stratigraphic relationships.
Construct geological maps, cross-sections, and other spatial representations that integrate field data and geological interpretations.
Analyse structural and sedimentological data during fieldwork to create first order interpretations on geological relationships and regional deformation processes.
Integrate geological field observations and first order interpretations to reconstruct the geological and tectonic evolution of a study area.
Synthesise field observations with published geological data to evaluate and effectively communicate the regional and broader geological context of the study area.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EART2008 Sedimentary Geology 2/EART2009 Structural Geology 2/EART2010 Igneous and Metamorphic Geology 2

title: Measurement
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip learners with knowledge and skills required for the practice of quantity surveying. The course introduces cost management principles and appropriate knowledge in respect to standard methods of measurement, preparation of bills of quantities, and measurement of building and civil works. The learners will develop analytical thinking and effective communication skills for quantity surveying practice. This course aligns with the program’s intent to excel learners to become a successful professional in the construction industry by applying knowledge and skills to quantify and apply costs for building and infrastructure projects.
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of the Quantity Surveyor in a multi-disciplinary project team
Read and interpret construction drawings, specifications and codes
Understand and apply standard phraseology related to building and civil work trades
Apply standard method of measurement to measure building and civil trade packages
Demonstrate the ability to perform computerised measurement and billing

title: Field Palaeontology 3
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with an in-depth theoretical and practical understanding of the techniques and steps involved in the search, survey, excavation, preparation, curation and management of invertebrate and vertebrate fossils and sites.
learning_outcomes: Recognise sedimentary deposits capable of preserving fossils and apply the principal elements of fossil excavation
Apply the principles of fossil excavation in the field and understand the multidisciplinary nature of modern palaeontology.
Understand and apply how to collect and annotate data (context recording), prepare, preserve and catalogue fossils in the field.
Describe the diversity and chronological context of South Australia’s palaeontological heritage.
Communicate aspects of palaeontological discovery and heritage to their peers and the community in accessible language
prerequisites: Must have completed 1 of BIOL2022 Evolutionary Biology 2/EART2008 Sedimentary Geology 2

assessment_tasks.task_name: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions

title: Construction Environmental Science
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course will demonstrate the physical principles used in the design and management of buildings to create environmentally suitable and sustainable conditions, including the following: Psychrometry and thermal comfort. Admission and exclusion of solar radiation. Resultant temperature, design heat loss/gain, natural ventilation and thermal insulation. Thermal modelling software. Energy efficiency, life cycle energy concepts, greenhouse gas emissions and other environmental considerations. Introduction to natural lighting design methods. Control of noise. Noise annoyance and the community. Water-efficient and water-resilient design. Relevant content of the National Construction Code, and of Green Star Design and As-built.
learning_outcomes: Apply climate parameters for maximum thermal comfort and minimum energy consumption in buildings.
Apply engineering principles to the passive design of environmentally suitable and sustainable conditions.
Understand the design of natural lighting and natural ventilation systems.
Communicate effectively with all stakeholders, concepts in sustainability in construction.
incompatibilities: must not have completed CIVE2015 UO Construction Environmental Science at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed CIVE2008 Construction Environmental Science at the University of South Australia

title: High-rise Construction
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills on the construction of high-riseBuildings, and will cover an array of topics such as a history of tall buildings, their structural elements including wind and seismic loading's through to handling of materials, people movement within the building, de-construction, sustainability and modular high rise construction.
learning_outcomes: Have an in-depth understanding of the history and evolution of high-rise buildings.
Critically review multi-story construction methods and materials used for the construction of high-rise buildings.
Gain an understanding of building dead and live loads, as well as seismic and wind loads on tall buildings.
Evaluate the logistics involved in the construction of a building such as materials handling, and people movement and the methods of demolishing a high-rise building.
Explore the use of smart building technology and sustainability of high-rise buildings.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of ARCH1010 Structures/BLDG1002 Low-rise Construction and Land Surveying
incompatibilities: Must not have completed CIVE3014

title: Risk, Quality and People Management
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: Students will build a deeper understanding of the management of construction projects with a particular emphasis on risk, quality, and people management.
learning_outcomes: Apply risk management theory to identify, analyse and evaluate risks in construction projects
Recommend alternative courses of action to manage, monitor and control risks in construction projects
Apply quality management theory to prepare quality management plans for construction projects
Demonstrate business management skills including personnel and resources management, leadership, and communication in construction businesses
Demonstrate professionalism, teamwork and effective communication as a construction management professional
prerequisites: must have completed BLDG1000 Introduction to Construction Management

title: Palaeontology and Palaeoenvironments 3
school: School of Phys, Chem and E Sci
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide an advanced understanding of modern palaeontology as a multidisciplinary subject spanning the interface between geology and biology.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in common practical skills in palaeontology and an ability to evaluate, interpret and communicate scientific results obtained from fossil deposits

Comprehend fossil formation processes in different environments, and recognise the importance of studying taphonomic histories and stratigraphic contexts to ensure reliable interpretations of fossil records

Evaluate changes in diversity and palaeoecology through time, assess how key extinction and evolutionary events have been driven by major geological and palaeoenvironmental change, and understand the role of applied palaeontology for future conservation efforts
Combine information from fossils and associated sedimentary archives to undertake multi-proxy interpretations of past environments, and assess how environmental conditions have changed through time
Demonstrate an understanding of key geochronology techniques and modern analytical approaches used to contextualise and interpret fossil records
Critically debate and evaluate current topics or controversies in palaeontology via group presentations and written reports
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of BIOL2022 Evolutionary Biology 2/EART2008 Sedimentary Geology 2

assessment_tasks.task_name: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis
Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions

title: Introduction to Structural Design - Loads and Forms
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the conceptual and preliminary stages of structural design including developing an understanding of the behaviour and typical use cases of common structural forms and the quantification of load paths and design actions arising from gravity, live loads, wind and earthquake loads.
learning_outcomes: Perform hand calculation methods to determine design actions on both determinate and indeterminate structural elements.
Apply approximate analysis and superposition techniques to convert loads into design actions.
Demonstrate comprehension of the behaviour of structures by performing qualitative structural analysis.
Apply computer software to perform structural analysis of different structural forms and verify the computer output with appropriate hand calculation methods.
Identify and quantify the loads acting on structures using AS1170.
Describe load paths within a structure and calculate loads and design actions on structural elements as the loads are transferred through a structure.
Dimension structural members to comply with limit state design criteria.
prerequisites: Must have completed ENGM1000 Introduction to Engineering Mechanics
incompatibilities: Must not have completed CIVE 2009 - Civil Engineering Techniques at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed CIVILENG2002 - Structural Mechanics at the University of Adelaide

assessment_tasks.task_name: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task

title: OL Health care systems: structure, policy and people
syllabus_overview: This is a time of major change in our health care system. The system must meet the health needs of all Australians at a time when health care costs are rapidly increasing and our population is ageing. How can we ensure our health care system is efficient, equitable and the expectations of all Australians are met? In this course, students will examine how our health care system currently works and explore the various strategies that could improve both the quality and effectiveness of the care that people receive. This will include studying health care policies and how they directly impact on people's lives; following the health care journeys of a variety of Australians to examine how the health care system functions at an individual level and how it interacts with other systems and we will look briefly at how health care systems in other countries work. Students will learn a variety of practical skills such as how to analyse health polices, how to write a policy brief and how to approach health care reform.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding and analyse current public health issues and controversies and critique the different public policy responses to health issues within Australia and internationally.
Demonstrate understanding of, and describe how, the Australian health care system works.
Review and critique public health policies and strategies.
Map patient journeys through different parts of the health system, including acute care, primary care, rural health services and Indigenous health services.
Develop specific oral and written communications, informed by appropriate evidence, to effectively communicate health care issues and research results to policy makers.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed PUBHLTH2508OUA Health care systems - structure, policy and people at the University of Adelaide

title: Construction Engineering
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course will introduce students to construction engineering. The content of the course includes project delivery methods, first principles estimating, cost planning and scheduling, contracts and specifications. This course will feature guest speakers from the construction industry and will also visit a construction site, which will form the basis of the major project that underpins this course. The ability to read and interpret drawings is a key learning outcome of this course. Students will also be introduced to methods of construction associated with earthworks, concrete and steel.
learning_outcomes: Explain contractual arrangements that may be adopted in the construction industry
Explain how the estimation process is influenced by the transfer of risk for different project delivery methods
Identify how a project scope is broken up into a series of trade packages for construction
Estimate construction timelines and costs
Read and interpret technical engineering drawings
Prepare a site visit report to a professional standard

title: Honours Biomedicine Research Project Part 1
school: School of Pharm and Biomed Sci
syllabus_overview: This course forms the main basis of an honours project conducted in the School of Biomedicine. Students will be expected to engage in a novel, independent research project under the guidance of a principal supervisor and co-supervisor(s)focussed on key research areas in Anatomy, Pathology, Pharmacology, Physiology, or Reproduction and Development. To complete the course, students will be required to prepare and deliver a project proposal and resource pro-forma. This course provides an advanced insight into the scientific research process and develops professional attributes and skills.
learning_outcomes: Execute a well-defined research project, under the guidance of a project supervisor.
Critically interpret the background literature relevant to the research project.

Demonstrate mastery of the techniques required for the experimental study of a research question,including collection, storage, and evaluation of data which is rigorous and methodical in accordancewith the Australian Code for Responsible Practice of Research.
Identify and evaluate methodological or technical issues in a research project and define the importantelements required to solve them.
Communicate the elements of the research project clearly and concisely in spoken and written English.
corequisites: Must be enrolled in HLTH4005 Honours Foundation Research Skills
incompatibilities: Must not have completed all of HLTH1035 Honours Biomedicine Research Project Part 1/HLTHSC4510A Honours Biomedicine Research Project Part 1 at the University of Adelaide

title: Mobile Game Development
syllabus_overview: Utilise a recognised game development methodology and game engine to design and implement a mobile-platform game. Students will collaborate in creating engaging game mechanics using touch inputs and apply user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) principles targeting mobile devices.
learning_outcomes: Work effectively in teams in the development of a game targeting mobile platforms.
Design and implement mobile game mechanics that use touch inputs using a game engine.
Develop user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) principles in mobile game development.
Integrate sound, graphics, and animations into a mobile game using a game engine.
Test and optimise games for performance and compatibility on several devices.
Develop a compelling pitch including a live reliable demonstration for a new mobile game and justify it meets the demands of a significant market segment.
prerequisites: must have completed all of COMP2021 Software Development Practice/COMP2039 Game Engines

title: Construction Management and Technology 1
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to manage following critical aspects of construction management: sustainability, construction safety and procurement. Following a life cycle approach, this course provides opportunities to have a comprehensive understanding of impacts of construction activities and procurement approaches on the safety and sustainability performance of construction projects. By learning principles in lectures and practicing in tutorials, students will develop critical skills on managing these key aspects of construction management. This course aligns with the program's intent to prepare future leaders of the construction industry that have to deal with critical challenges in environmental and social impacts of construction project, safety hazards and alternative procurement strategies.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate various procurement routes and select the appropriate procurement method for building and infrastructure projects
Critically examine safety related challenges and corresponding measures for building and infrastructure projects
Identify and manage stakeholders in the construction sector and the project environment
Identify key principles of sustainable development and the role of sustainable construction technologies
Critically examine the resource efficiency issues (e.g. reuse and recycled materials, energy efficiency) in building and infrastructure projects
Demonstrate the understanding of using life cycle approach to manage construction projects

assessment_tasks.task_name: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions

title: Internship PG
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to encourage Engineering students to reflect on their internship experience/s and demonstrate how exposure to a professional environment has helped to develop a range of professional competencies and employability skills. Students will align internship tasks and objectives to the Engineers Australia Stage 1 competencies and consider individual strengths and areas for personal improvement by reflecting on what they have discovered about themselves throughout their study experience.
learning_outcomes: Apply project management techniques to devise and synthesize engineering solutions to complex open-ended problems
Design and execute the proposed activities and/or tasks to answer the questions and problems as required
Demonstrate ability to apply engineering methods and processes within the specialised discipline (e.g. operations, facilities, equipment, software, design, research)
Provide insight to the breadth and depth of competencies expected for a professional engineer
Communicate effectively and professionally, in writing and verbally, engineering concepts and information to both technically informed and lay domains
Demonstrate ability to work cooperatively as a team member, contributing to team leadership as the situation requires and where appropriate
incompatibilities: must not have completed ENG7110 Internship PG at the University of Adelaide

title: Introductory Flying
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: To provide students with an introduction to the areas of aviation knowledge required for the commencement of flight training.
learning_outcomes: Execute aircraft operation in a safe and legally compliant manner.
Demonstrate aeronautical knowledge sufficiently to meet the professional standard of solo aircraft operation.
Demonstrate good decision making, situational awareness, and airmanship by responding to simulated or real in-flight emergencies.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed AERO2061 Introductory Flying at the University of South Australia

title: Enterprise Networks
syllabus_overview: This course aims to develop the knowledge and skills required to support implementing and troubleshooting advanced routing technologies and services in enterprise networks. Building upon concepts developed, this course delves into advanced routing, multi-casting, quality of service operations, virtual private networking, infrastructure services and network management. This course aligns with the intent of the program to develop networking professionals.
learning_outcomes: Identify and configure advanced routing solutions to satisfy complex networking requirements
Analyse multicast and quality of service operations in an enterprise network
Demonstrate the skills required to configure and troubleshoot virtual private networks and related technologies
Use network and device management tools and troubleshoot related issues
Investigate, diagnose, and rectify routing problems in enterprise networks
Document an implementation plan which includes determining the most appropriate design parameters including routing and other advanced protocols
prerequisites: must have completed COMP2020 Network Design

title: Construction Communication and Digital Construction Fundamentals
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide learners with a deep understanding of communication tools in construction, integrating manual drafting, Revit, and BIM alongside ISO 19650 and RIBA Plan of Work. Through immersive experiences with virtual reality, students develop effective verbal, written, and visual communication skills, fostering teamwork and autonomy. emphasising problem-solving, ethical conduct, and sustainable development, learners cultivate critical thinking, research skills, and environmental awareness crucial for professional practice. The course addresses problem-solving, understanding others' needs, ethical actions, and effective communication, while fostering skills in communication, critical thinking, and technological competence.
learning_outcomes: Understanding the communication processes and core activities for traditional and digital construction projects based on the RIBA Plan of Work and the ISO 19650 standards to convey project information effectively across stakeholders with precision and alignment

Develop effective stakeholder engagement plans integrating verbal, written, and 2D drawings/3D visual communication skills for informed decision-making and progress monitoring throughout project lifecycles, ensuring comprehensive strategic alignment
Examine collaboration approaches among construction stakeholders, considering client needs and BIM advancements, to enhance productivity with a deep understanding and critical evaluation

Demonstrate proficient use of innovative technologies, especially BIM, in construction projects to achieve productivity, efficiency, and sustainability goals, while upholding ethical and legal standards
incompatibilities: Must not have completed BUIL 1021 Construction Communication at the University of South Australia

assessment_tasks.task_name: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions

title: International Development Practice: Design Project
syllabus_overview: This independent research-based course builds on practical courses in the major and enables students to immerse themselves fully in a program design exercise. In the initial weeks students refresh their understanding of key aspects of program design, such as setting objectives, defining development problems, developing monitoring and evaluation frameworks/log frames. Student groups work on a range of collective skills-building activities before moving on to think about their own individual project/program design submissions. The comprehensive design document is developed in a context and upon a theme of the students own choice. This work will be supported by ongoing presentations and periodic supervision.
learning_outcomes: In-depth knowledge of international development practice
In-depth practical experience of applying development tools and methods to real-world problems
In-depth knowledge of project/program management processes
Fully able to apply critical thinking skills to development problems
Strong skills in communication, collaborative enquiry and problem solving
Able to foster an awareness of ethical, social, and cultural issues within a global context and their importance in the exercise of professional skills and responsibilities
prerequisites: Must have completed POLI2005 How to Change the World: Practicing Development

title: Project Management Research Study
syllabus_overview: The Project Management Research Study is the program's capstone course requiring students to deliver a detailed research report based on their nominated field of interest. The research study will follow standard research processes including topic selection and introduction, literature review, research methodology, results analysis and discussion, conclusion and recommendations. The course is intended to develop student research skills and enhance understanding within their field of interest.
learning_outcomes: Critically review relevant academic literature to identify current and emerging issues in project management
Identify and apply appropriate research methodologies
Collect, analyse and interpret research data to formulate conclusions and recommendations
Explain and defend research outcomes using both oral and written presentations
prerequisites: must have completed PROJ3002 PM Research Methods

title: Constructive Journalism
school: School of Comm, Media and Jour
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with a comprehensive introduction to constructive journalism. Students will explore and analyse emerging constructive approaches such as solutions journalism, restorative narrative, Indigenous reporting, peace journalism, reciprocal journalism, future-oriented reporting, and solidarity journalism. After exploring the ethical basis of constructive journalism and its intersections with social justice, diverse communities, and society, students will apply what they have learned to constructive journalism production.
learning_outcomes: Articulate how constructive journalism approaches shift away from traditional, and western hegemonic, journalism practices and analyse and their role in society
Evaluate techniques of constructive journalism in a range of news contexts, mediums, and within diverse communities
Analyse theoretical and ethical underpinnings of emerging forms of constructive journalism
Apply the techniques of constructive journalism to journalism practice by creating original work underpinned by the theoretical and ethical considerations of the emerging genre
Participate and collaborate in newsroom settings, peer-reviews, and reflect on constructive journalistic practices
prerequisites: Must have completed JOUR1007 Audio Journalism
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in MDIA2022 Media Law, Policy and Ethics

title: Digital Technologies
syllabus_overview: The course aims to familiarise students with key Digital Technologies concepts and content as outlined in relevant curricula. Students will develop their knowledge, understanding, and practical skills in planning and implementing digital technology-based learning experiences for students from Foundation to Year 6.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of concepts, structure and content within the Digital Technologies subject
Plan and design teaching resources to enhance students’ Digital Technologies knowledge, understanding and practice of processes and skills
Develop, apply and critically reflect on the skills and resources required to support teaching in the Digital Technologies learning area
Design effective digital technologies learning experiences for children in Foundation to Year 6, demonstrating understanding of curriculum requirements and innovative teaching strategies

title: Big Data Analysis & Industry Project
syllabus_overview: In this course, students will complete a medium-scale, industry-inspired, data science project. This project will involve evaluating, selecting and applying relevant data science techniques, principles and theory to a data science problem. Working with a real-world, industry-motivated dataset, students will develop their data science skills and knowledge and demonstrate autonomy, initiative and accountability. Students will need to reflect on the nature of their data and identify any social and ethical concerns and identify appropriate ethical frameworks for data management. As part of the course students will deliver a written and oral presentation of their project design, plan, methodologies, and outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Apply data analysis principles and theory to process and analyse real world big data
Evaluate data analysis techniques by applying real world datasets using benchmark metrics
Develop algorithms based on learnt techniques for the statistical analysis of big data
Identify project goals; develop project milestones and execute them accordingly
Analyse known industry studies and simulate assessment by following industry standards

title: Advanced Concepts in Ecology 3
syllabus_overview: In this course students will understand and apply advanced ecological concepts, building on knowledge and concepts from Principles of Ecology 2. To do so, we explore conceptual and mechanistic models that aim to understand the dynamics of biological populations, communities and ecosystems. We then apply these models in a range of theoretical and applied scenarios in workshops. A mandatory field camp provides learners with hands-on experience and practical job-ready skills necessary for applying ecological principles in real-world environments. This course provides a crucial theoretical and applied understanding of ecological concepts for understanding the processes determining biodiversity in nature and its relevance for conservation and management.This course includes a compulsory field camp in the mid-semester break (see timetable). The field trips for Advanced Concepts in Ecology 3 and Freshwater Ecology 3 courses are scheduled back-to-back so that students can do both. Note that there is an additional cost associated with the camp, which varies year-to-year but is approximately 200-250 dollars.
learning_outcomes: Explain and synthesise fundamental and advanced ecological concepts.
Analyse and evaluate complex ecological patterns and processes using contemporary conceptual and quantitative models.
Formulate specific research questions and design corresponding study designs to address existing knowledge gaps in ecology, both collaboratively and independently.
Collect high-quality ecological data in field settings and analyse using appropriate methods.
Communicate and justify ecological findings in relation to the broader scientific literature.
prerequisites: must have completed BIOL2051 Principles of Ecology 2

title: Off-Earth Construction
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The aim of the Off-Earth Construction course is to familiarise students with the various environments and subsequent challenges for engineers to design systems, materials, and methodologies to build, inspect, and maintain infrastructure off-planet. Driven by real-world events that will soon see humans returning to the Moon and the construction of several lunar bases by multiple nations, in addition to other companies and nations with demonstrated intent to settle Mars and/or construct large space habitats, this course puts into practical terms much of the previous coursework to understand how to actually facilitate the construction of off-Earth infrastructure (landing pads, roads, berms, foundations, etc).
learning_outcomes: Discuss current space construction plans and requirements
Demonstrate a specialist understanding of the various near-term deep space environments
Summarise what in-situ resources are, abundances, and potential uses in construction
Design a construction pathway for a self-selected off-Earth infrastructure element
Demonstrate proficiency in practical lab skills relevant to working with off-Earth regolith simulants
Explain the infrastructure requirements of both crewed and uncrewed off-Earth facilities

title: UO Engineering Materials
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to provide students with an introduction to the relationship between microstructure, properties and processing of engineering materials. The course will also introduce students to appropriate selection of materials for engineering applications. The course will introduce students to the properties of engineering materials, and provide them with an understanding of how these properties are measured. Mechanical, electrical, magnetic, physical and surface properties will be examined. The primary failure modes of engineering materials, corrosion, fatigue and wear will be studied. The structure of materials will be studied at the atomic scale, the micro scale and the macro scale. The four main classes of materials will be included in the course: ceramics, polymers, metals, and composites.
learning_outcomes: Explain the relationship between microstructure and material properties for a broad range of material classes.
Analyse and interpret basic engineering data and measurements.
Utilise material properties in basic problem solving in the context of civil, electrical, and mechanical engineering.
incompatibilities: must not have completed RENG1006 UO Engineering Materials at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed RENG1005 Engineering Materials at the University of South Australia

title: Game Engines
syllabus_overview: Equip students with the practical skills and knowledge and to develop a video game using a modern game engine. Students will explore engine architecture, apply artificial intelligence concepts, and develop immersive environments, culminating in the creation and deployment of a multi-platform video game.
learning_outcomes: Explain the fundamental concepts and architecture of modern game engines
Analyse the use of engine techniques within games
Apply artificial intelligence concepts within a game engine
Develop multi-level environments using game engines
Build and deploy games across multiple platforms
prerequisites: Must have completed all of COMP1005 Object-Oriented Programming/INFO2020 Visual Asset Design for Games
incompatibilities: Must not have completed INFT3032 Game Engines at the University of South Australia

title: UO Electrical Circuit Analysis
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to provide students with a firm foundation in electrical DC and AC circuit analysis, and the ability to use computer software for circuit simulation and analysis. This course will build on the basic principles of electrical and electronic theories. The course will introduce circuit analysis techniques such as nodal analysis, mesh analysis, linearity and superposition techniques, Thevenin and Norton Theorems. The course will introduce second order transients and move into steady state power analysis, magnetically coupled networks and polyphase circuits. Eventuating with exploring variable frequency network performance, frequency response and the relationship of poles zeros on the bode plots. The course will introduce the use of computer-based tools for design and circuit analysis.
learning_outcomes: Explain the concept of AC circuits, AC power and phasor representation of AC signals.
Apply various circuit solving techniques and theorems to analyse steady state and transient response of basic electrical circuits.
Identify circuit transfer function, sketch Bode plots and analyse behaviour of variable frequency circuits.
Design and perform experiments and apply computer software for circuit modelling and simulation, and for processing and representation of data.
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of ENGE1002 UO Electrical and Electronic Systems/ENGE1012 Electrical and Electronic Systems (UniSA) AND must have completed 1 of MATH1032 UO Mathematical Methods for Engineers 2/MATH1058 Mathematical Methods for Engineers 2
incompatibilities: must not have completed EEET1028 UO Electrical Circuit Analysis at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EEET1003 Electrical Circuit Analysis at the University of South Australia

title: Construction Contract Management: Performance, Quality & Disputes
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course will provide students with contract knowledge and analytical skills for commercial management of construction projects in relation to latent conditions, subcontracting, insurances, defective building works, security, contract termination and insolvency, claims and dispute resolution. The course includes Site conditions and latent Conditions; Defective building works; Indemnities and insurances. Subcontracting; Contract security; Contract termination and Insolvency; Dispute resolution clauses in construction contracts; Claims and disputes; Litigation and arbitration; Alternative dispute resolution methods.
learning_outcomes: Identify, explain and apply the clauses in construction contracts which deal with performance security, subcontracting and people, property and the works
Identify, explain and apply the clauses in construction contracts which deal with latent conditions and defective works and discuss associated claims together with relevant case law and legislation
Explain the rights of parties with respect to termination of contract and insolvency under construction contracts and discuss associated claims together with relevant case law and legislation

Distinguish between extra-contractual claims & claims under construction contracts and describe contractual dispute resolution procedures & the alternative dispute resolution methods commonly used in the construction industry.

title: Applied Machine Learning UG
syllabus_overview: This course surveys the practical application of machine learning in modern organisations and society. You will learn processes for tool-selection based on requirements and available resources; verifying and validating discovered models and how to apply results in real environments; and information resources for tracking technological advances.

Select an appropriate method and tool for a given problem and data set
Distinguish problems and data sets that are amenable to machine learning methods from those that are not

title: Masters Research Theory and Practice
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to provide students with an advanced understanding of the nature of knowledge and its pursuit through research and to equip them with the skills to demonstrate autonomy, expert judgement, adaptability and responsibility as a researcher. Philosophy of knowledge, nature of reality, ethics and research, ontology, epistemology, knowledge claims and intellectual paradigms, research design, confidence and reliability, research methods (quantitative and qualitative), data analysis and interpretation and proposal writing.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on theory and professional research practice.
Demonstrate skills in investigating, analysing and synthesizing complex research concepts and information.
Critique a substantial body of relevant literature.
Devise a rigorous research or investigative methodology and attendant research methods.
As a professional, design an international quality research-based proposal.

title: Aircraft Navigation 2
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: In this course, students will carry out cross country flight and aircraft handling to successfully pass the Commercial Pilot Licence Flight Test. Flight planning, performance and preparation; departure and entry procedures controlled and in controlled aerodromes; diversions and simulated in-flight emergencies; flight outside and within controlled airspace; en route navigation under visual flight rules (VFR).
learning_outcomes: Operate the aircraft en-route VFR utilising the RNAV, VOR, GPS and autopilot.

Demonstrate a professional attitude consistent with an airline pilot applying: good decision making, situational awareness, airmanship and threat and error management by recognising and avoiding potential conflict, deviation from normal operations. Respond correctly to simulated or real in -flight emergencies.

Navigate the aircraft en route, at low level and in reduced visibility. Perform lost and diversion procedures. Execute departure and arrival procedures. Operations will be conducted within controlled and uncontrolled airspace. All exercises to be conducted within the CASA prescribed Commercial Pilot Licence flight test tolerances.

title: Introduction to Water Engineering
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course dives into the essentials of water engineering, crucial for civil and environmental engineers, covering a broad range of topics. You'll explore the water cycle, hydrological processes, and fluid mechanics, including hydrostatics, buoyancy, and fluid motion. Building on these fundamentals, we will then dive into pipe flow concepts and master open channel hydraulics. Practical applications are emphasized through a design project, bringing pipeline and open channel flow principles to life.
learning_outcomes: Perform a basic hydrological assessment for a given catchment system, including the collection, analysis and interpretation of appropriate data, and communicate findings.
Apply principles of fluid statics and fluid motion to solve problems related to forces on immersed bodies and steady flow.
Apply the underlying governing principles for behaviour of flows and pressures to solve problems related to simple pipe systems.
Identify and apply the relevant governing principles to solve problems related to open channel flow for simple channel geometries.
Undertake laboratory experiments competently and safely on a range of foundational fluid, pipe and open channel systems, and employ the appropriate theory to analyse and interpret the measured data.
Analyse, design and optimise selected water resource systems, including communication of designs and design choices, recognising uncertainty and limitations of engineering approaches and systems.

title: Computation for Materials Engineering
syllabus_overview: This course provides an introduction to modelling and simulation of materials, covering force-field based atomistic and molecular simulation, and first principle calculation based on quantum mechanics. Students will learn how to use computation as new tools to predict functional material properties. Students will also learn how to design materials and structures from the bottom up - to make lighter, stronger, more efficient, and less expensive materials. In this subject, students will get hands-on training in both the fundamentals and applications of these exciting new methods to key engineering problems, such as energy, optical, and quantum.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of theories for computation, such as force field methods and quantum mechanics
Demonstrate knowledge of modern computation techniques for materials engineering
Understand the capability and limitation of computation techniques for materials engineering
Understand the architecture of high-performance-computing (HPC) facilities
Apply computation techniques to model specific chemical and physical properties of materials for energy, optical, or quantum applications
Apply basic scripting to facilitate and accelerate the modelling of materials

title: Branding

Students will learn about how consumers process, store, and retrieve brand-related information. They will develop a clear understanding of the key brand performance metrics and benchmarks for your brand and come to understand how brands compete.
learning_outcomes: Examine marketing knowledge from the perspective of brand management
Compare the quality of evidence available to support branding theories
Demonstrate international perspectives and an ability to discuss the suitability of evidence-based brand growth recommendations for specific market conditions.

title: Applied Aerodynamics
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the fundamentals and practical aspects of incompressible and compressible flows and the design and operation of flow systems, including pipe networks, automobiles and flight vehicles. The course content includes: flow of inviscid and viscous fluids; laminar and turbulent flow in pipes and boundary layers; losses in pipe systems; lift and drag forces on moving bodies, aerofoil theory; incompressible-flow machines; fundamentals of compressible flow; 1-D compressible pipe flow; compressible flow nozzles; Rayleigh flow; Fanno flow; external compressible flow around bodies including transonic and supersonic vehicles; design considerations; experimental techniques.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the fundamental principles of incompressible and compressible fluid mechanics and aerodynamics
Apply these principles to real systems such as pipe flows, automobiles and aircraft
Explain current practice in the areas of fluid mechanics and aerodynamics
Discuss some aspects of fluid mechanics and aerodynamics
Use problem solving and analytical skills
Explain the principles underlying sustainable flow system design
prerequisites: must have completed ENGM2014 Thermo-Fluids I

Compare and contrast the different system architectures.

title: Building Services (UniSA)
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is for students to discover the scientific principles used in the design and management of enclosed environments in residential and commercial buildings. Application of physical principles to the maintenance of conditions within buildings. Thermal comfort, heat load analysis, air conditioning processes, plant selection and sizing. Implications for managing the construction process. Gas, oil, electricity and solid fuels. Design of hot and cold water supply, drainage systems and effluent, electrical supply and distribution systems and vertical transportation. Introduction to building services.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the scientific principles which underpin the operation of specific building service engineering functions.
Interpret the design and operation of supply services in domestic and commercial construction.

Assess the design and operation of conditioning and providing adequate amenity of internal environments and other engineering services systems in commercial buildings and the implications that such systems have in the construction process.

title: Cost Planning and Management

This includes cost planning and detailed estimating, business management, company management (accounting, cash flow), commercial management, and professional practice. The learners will develop analytical thinking, effective communication and economic consideration and interpretation skills required for a cost management profession. This course aligns with the program’s intent to excel learners to become leading professionals in the construction industry.
learning_outcomes: Discuss cost management principles throughout construction project stages
Apply cost planning techniques and economic factors throughout the design process of construction projects
Apply knowledge on estimating for tender submissions from a contracting standpoint
Analyse financial performance at the business and the project levels
Apply knowledge of management techniques at the business and project levels
Demonstrate ethical behaviour and professionalism in lifelong learning and diverse work settings

learning_outcomes: Understand the terminology, characteristics, and scientific and engineering properties of principal construction materials, along with other factors influencing their selection and performance
Identify and report on the appropriate and best practice application and installation requirements of construction materials and components
Demonstrate understanding of climate parameters and passive building designs for indoor environmental quality and energy efficiency
Explain the integration of renewable energy, water-efficient features, and noise control measures in buildings
Explore sustainable building innovations and communicate sustainability concepts to stakeholders

Understand the environmental impact of steel construction and apply this knowledge to the design of steel structures

title: The Individual in Society

title: Engineering Capstone Experience A
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course will enable graduates to develop the skills required by engineering professionals in negotiating, planning, designing, constructing, implementing, testing and reporting engineering developments, schemes or designs. The course will utilise real projects provided by industry with industrial representatives acting as clients to the students. Different developments or projects will be offered each year. Students will first develop a tender and then produce a feasibility study for the development. The course is undertaken by the class acting as consulting companies with the management and organisation of that company being the responsibility of the students. Regular meetings with the lecturers and industry clients will review progress and guide the teams in the projects. Significant emphasis will be placed on the social, environmental, international, political and economic contexts applicable to each project.
learning_outcomes: Determine and respond to client requirements through application of engineering knowledge, techniques, established engineering methods, design and project management processes. (PO 1, 3, 4, 5, 9) (EA 1.3, 1.5, 1.6, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4)

Students will develop the skills necessary to analyse, evaluate, and implement Industry 4.0 solutions within organisational contexts, fostering innovation and competitiveness. This course aligns with the program goals by fostering engineering knowledge, complex problem-solving abilities, and the capacity for professional communication and teamwork in the context of emergent technological paradigms.

Apply materials and process selection, design for manufacturing and assembly, and failure modes and effect analysis, the key technical elements in Industry 4.0

Demonstrate skills to analytically and numerically solve problems related to aerospace propulsion systems both on paper and using numerical methods

andDemonstrate skills in planning and presentation of scientific talks and reports

title: UO Programming Concepts
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to develop problem solving skills and core programming techniques to acquire and process real-world data related to civil, electrical, mechanical and other engineering problems. This course allows students to develop an understanding of fundamental programming concepts and the relevance of programming in solving engineering problems. These concepts will be applied through design and implementation of programming code and the use of microcontrollers. The course also covers coding standards and good programming practices, as well as problem solving processes and tools.Programming concepts covered in this course include: representing data (data types, variables, constants); math and Boolean expressions (relational, equality and Boolean operators); control constructs (sequence, selection, iteration); using and writing functions (call by value and call by reference); arrays (1-D and 2-D); strings; pointers; dynamic memory allocation; structures; array of structures; multi-file programs; standard and file input and output. Programming integrated development environments (for both C and microcontrollers) will be used.
learning_outcomes: Apply problem solving strategies to move from a problem statement to a code solution.
Implement, test and debug programs using the C programming language and choose appropriate conditional and iteration constructs for a given programming task.
Analyse and explain the behaviour of programs.
Program a microcontroller to perform a simple task relevant to a civil, electrical, mechanical or other engineering problem.
Apply good programming practices, specifically, international coding style standards and source code documentation.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMP1045 Programming Concepts at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed COMP1047 UO Programming Concepts at the University of South Australia

assessment_tasks.task_name: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Oral Defence

title: Statistics for Human Factors
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip students with essential statistical methods and analytical tools vital for human factors research. The focus is on developing robust understanding and skills in executing various statistical tests, from foundational concepts to advanced analysis techniques. By learning topics such as descriptive statistics, null hypothesis significance testing, programming with statistics software packages, data visualization, parametric and non-parametric methods, and advanced topics like regression, latent variable analysis, and General Linear Model, students will be prepared to conduct rigorous and meaningful research in human factors, ensuring they can effectively analyse data, and interpret results within real-world applications.
learning_outcomes: Describe fundamental statistical principles for human factor research.
Analyse the results from practical statistical tests commonly used in human factor research.
Apply statistical computing software to perform data manipulation, execute various statistical tests, and create impactful visualisations.
Examine research designs and data quality, using statistical techniques and measures to ensure research standards.
prerequisites: must have completed COMP1005 Object-Oriented Programming

title: Clinical Podiatry Practice 201
syllabus_overview: In this course, students will develop skills in the theory and practical application of podiatry assessment and treatment techniques. Regional foot pain and pathologies, diabetes related foot concerns, infection of soft tissue and bone, fractures of bone, oedema of the lower limb, management for acute dermatological foot pathologies; advanced examination technique: vascular, neurological; clinical techniques: nail treatment, scalpel techniques, equipment handling, safety; mechanical techniques: use of padding and strapping; dressing techniques; topical medicaments: choice, safe handling and application, patient instructions, recording.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate safe and professional clinical behaviour, verbal and written communication skills with patients, clinical staff and other practitioners including the use of ISBAR handover, consistent to a beginner level.
Discuss and apply the appropriate clinical reasoning processes to the assessment and treatment management of simple foot related disorders and pathologies
Apply constructs of person-centred and professional practice that supports safe recommendations or prescription of S2, S3 and S4 pharmaceutical products.
Discuss common musculoskeletal pathologies affecting the foot and lower-limb and their aetiology
Communicate in a culturally safe, empathetic manner appropriate for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.
prerequisites: must have completed PODI2002 Clinical Podiatry Practice 200
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in PODI2003 Podiatry Studies 201
incompatibilities: must not have completed REHB2037 Clinical Podiatry Practice 201 at the University of South Australia

title: UO Object Oriented Programming
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to translate a problem description into a robust object oriented program. The aim of this course is topics covered in this course include: the programming environment, object oriented approaches to program design and development, object concepts and class design, testing, inheritance and polymorphism, and exceptions.
learning_outcomes: Convert a problem statement into an object oriented solution.
Use inheritance and polymorphism to solve problems.
Debug and fix code defects.
Apply international coding style standards.
Plan and conduct testing of software.
Analyse and explain the behaviour of object oriented programs.
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of COMP1021 UO Problem Solving and Programming/COMP1036 Problem Solving and Programming (UniSA)
incompatibilities: must not have completed COMP1048 Modelling and Analysis of Complex Systems OR must not have completed COMP1046 Special Topics in Computer Science A
