The course covers the topics of sound wave description and propagation, noise control techniques, the hearing mechanism, acoustic instrumentation, noise criteria, psychoacoustics, sound source types and radiated sound fields, outdoor sound propagation, sound power measurement techniques, sound in enclosed spaces, sound transmission loss, acoustic enclosures, acoustic barriers, pipe lagging and reactive and dissipative mufflers.
learning_outcomes: Apply acoustics concepts, definitions and theories to analysis of acoustic systems
Assess complex occupational and environmental noise problems using acceptable noise assessment standards, policies and criteria
Operate instrumentation for noise measurement and select the type of measurements appropriate for various situations
Recognise the importance of excessive noise and how it damages the hearing mechanism, and the responsibility of engineers to protect the community and provide a safe healthy environment
Perform analysis to predict the noise produced by various sources of sound and design practical noise control treatments
prerequisites: must have completed ENGMX300 Acoustics and Vibrations

assessment_tasks.task_name: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task

title: Green Infrastructure
school: School of Civil Eng & Cons Mgt
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide a practical introduction to the application of green infrastructure and water sensitive urban design (WSUD) in the built environment. The course will build on principles of hydrology and hydraulics to cover aspects of green infrastructure and WSUD, with an emphasis on water harvesting and vegetation. Students will learn about the function of green infrastructure and WSUD in (a) improving the sustainability of the urban water cycle and (b) reducing ‘urban heat islands’ and will engage in water-sensitive design practices covering simple, small-scale approaches at residential sites to more complex systems operated at municipal scales.
learning_outcomes: Define problems within conventional urban environments that cause urban heat islands and excess runoff, and articulate how well-designed green infrastructure addresses these problems
Seek, interpret and apply recommendations of current guidelines related to the planning, design, operation and maintenance of green infrastructure measures
Design and optimise flood management and rainwater/stormwater harvesting systems at different scales, from individual residential sites to municipal schemes.

Use appropriate calculations to determine vegetation water demands, design selected green infrastructure installations, and estimate the impact on water harvesting efficiency and urban cooling potential from transpiration.
Develop knowledge and skills in the application of water-sensitive principles to identify opportunities for inserting green infrastructure into the urban landscape
incompatibilities: Must not have completed CIVE5085 Green Infrastructure at the University of South Australia

title: VFX Placement: Compositing and Tracking
syllabus_overview: This immersive full semester course, delivered on-site at Rising Sun Pictures, will build upon students’ existing visual effects knowledge, and familiarises students with professional practice in the visual effects industry, providing the theory, skills, and techniques to produce industry-standard compositing and layout projects. Students will be able to demonstrate advanced skills in plate preparation, rotoscoping, and 3D tracking. Students will also develop a completed showreel and resume in addition to gaining practical hands-on experience with industry mentoring.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard compositing and tracking production practices.
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality composited film sequences.
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality tracked film sequences.
Plan and effectively manage a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline, through iterative project submission and review.
prerequisites: Must have completed 72 units of study in the Bachelor of Visual Effects or PD approval
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM3082-Visual Effects Placement Compositing and Tracking at the University of South Australia

title: Compositing Production Project
syllabus_overview: This immersive industry based course, delivered on-site at Rising Sun Pictures, will build upon students’ existing visual effects knowledge, and familiarises students with professional practice in the visual effects industry. In this course, and building on the skills developed in Plate Preparation Techniques and Introduction to 3D Tracking, students will undertake up to four advanced production projects that will emulate the processes of a production schedule. Students will be required to extend their paint, rotoscoping and tracking skills in order to produce a high quality, finished project for inclusion on their showreel, and to present to peers and RSP staff at the conclusion of the course. By the completion of the course, students will have acquired the skills required to produce industry standard 3D tracked film sequences.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard compositing production practices
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality composited and tracked film sequences
Demonstrate autonomy and adaptability in planning and managing a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline through iterative project submission and review
Demonstrate direction within a simulated team environment and produce work that meets industry-standard quality assurance and review processes
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM5070 Compositing Production Project at the University of South Australia

title: Cultural Interventions: Policy and Activism
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with a critical and historical understanding of cultural policy in Australia, different models of funding and government intervention through a series of national and global case studies. Students will learn how to evaluate cultural policy, question what constitutes an 'Australian Story' and who gets to tell them, and develop an understanding of the policy ecosystem surrounding them. Finally, students will develop an awareness of the relationship between policy and social change, examining various forms of activism and advocacy in the arts and cultural landscape.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the field and history of cultural and creative policy in Australia
Analyse cultural and creative policies in relation to the contexts of their emergence
Interpret and critique cultural and creative policy and its impacts
Discuss the relationships between policy, equity, diversity and social change
incompatibilities: Must not have completed HUMS1061 at the University of South Australia

title: Development Economics
school: School of Arch and Built Env
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide an introduction and overview of the urban development process. It explores the structure and organisation of the development industry and examines the production of urban development as a process. This exploration includes development feasibility studies including site and market analysis and regulatory and construction aspects. Emphasis is placed on the financial drivers of development and the methods employed to analyse urban development from a financial perspective, including an analysis of cost and value.A fundamental aim of the course is to help planners understand the mindset and technical approaches employed by developers of property so as to enable them to better negotiate desirable outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Perform a site analysis for an urban development site
Access and interpret planning information relevant to an urban site
Draft a quantified outline design for a development
Carry out a feasibility study of a development site
Apply appropriate techniques to the analysis of land and property value
Critically evaluate the development process in relation to an actual site with reference to the developer /planner interface

title: Mechanical Engineering Practice and Design Project
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course aims to familiarise the students with the practical aspects of professional mechanical engineering. Through presentations, hands-on activities, a design and construction project, and professional analysis, students will acquire and apply a diverse set of practical skills, including communication skills using engineering reports and graphical communication to design, fabricate, and operate small mechanisms. After completing this course, students will acquire basic knowledge of design principles for mechanical systems and mechanical design practice.
learning_outcomes: Develop fundamental practical knowledge and hands-on skills in mechanical engineering design and practice, with application to a design project.
Analyse and produce preliminary and detailed designs.
Produce, measure, analyse and assemble the designed components using relevant practical tools and software, and make performance-based revisions
Identify and analyse various mechanical mechanisms.
Effectively communicate engineering design knowledge in both written and graphical form.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of COMP1006 Engineering Programming/ENGI1001 Engineering Design and Prototyping/ENGI1002 Engineering Materials
incompatibilities: Must not have completed MECH ENG 2100 Design Practice at University of Adelaide

assessment_tasks.task_name: Skills Demonstration, Model, Model, Skills Demonstration

title: The Making of Modern Australia
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to examine the key social, economic and political events and turning points of the 20th and early 21st centuries that shaped who we are as Australians and how we interact with our global neighbours. The course places these events and turning points in context and chronological order beginning in the 1890s and proceeding to the present.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain key moments of economic, social and political change in Australia since the 1890s
Critically analyse the way in which ideas and assumptions about race, ethnicity, class and gender have shaped public policy in Australia
Produce effective written and/or oral arguments appropriate to the discipline of History and participate respectfully in team-based critical analysis and problem-solving

Demonstrate communication skills appropriate to career readiness, including use of online learning technologies, skills of collaborative and self-directed critical thinking, and sensitivity to the intercultural and ethical contexts of a diverse learning environment
prerequisites: Must have completed Completion of four level 1 subjects
incompatibilities: Must not have completed HIST2051-Australia and the World at the University of Adelaide

assessment_tasks.task_name: A range of assignments designed to support course outcomes

title: Introduction to 3D Tracking
syllabus_overview: This immersive industry based course, delivered on-site at Rising Sun Pictures, will build upon students’ existing visual effects knowledge, and familiarises students with professional practice in the visual effects industry. In this course, students will become familiar with tracking and layout techniques. Students will undertake up to ten production projects and develop familiarity and expertise with key layout and camera tracking techniques including scaling, building proxy geometry, matchmove rigging, camera export, lens distortion and survey registration. By the completion of the course, students will have acquired the skills required to produce industry standard 3D tracked film sequences.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard 3D tracking production practices.
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality 3D tracked film sequences.
Demonstrate autonomy and adaptability in planning and managing a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline through iterative project submission and review.
Demonstrate direction within a simulated team environment and produce work that meets industry-standard quality assurance and review processes.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM5072-Introduction to 3D Tracking at the University of South Australia

title: Plate Preparation Techniques
syllabus_overview: This immersive industry based course, delivered on-site at Rising Sun Pictures, will build upon students’ existing visual effects knowledge, and familiarises students with professional practice in the visual effects industry. In this course, students will be introduced to the preparation work required for scene set-up. Students will undertake up to eight production projects and develop familiarity and expertise with key visual effects techniques including rotoscope, paint, 2-D tracking, plate preparation and cleanup, and compositing. Students will gain skills needed to integrate, remove, isolate, grade and insert elements. By the completion of the course, students will have acquired the skills required to produce industry standard composited film sequences.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard compositing production practices.
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality composited film sequences.
Demonstrate autonomy and adaptability in planning and managing a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline through iterative project submission and review.
Demonstrate direction within a simulated team environment and produce work that meets industry-standard quality assurance and review processes.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM5071 Plate Preparation Techniques at the University of South Australia

title: UO Digital Media Project 2
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to apply and consolidate digital media studies and contexts to an innovative self-identified project. Students will identify and undertake a project applying digital skills and knowledge to establish connections between research and a range of digital media contexts including animation, collections and digital technologies.
learning_outcomes: integrate research and information to create effective and innovative responses to a range of digital media contexts
demonstrate a broadening understanding of issues related to innovative digital media practice
develop informative, interactive, coherent digital media material
prerequisites: Must have completed GRAP1018 UO Digital Media Project 1 AND must have completed 60 units from the XBDME program
incompatibilities: Must not have completed GRAP2036 UO Digital Media Project 2 at the University of South Australia

title: Honours Research 3 (Creative)
syllabus_overview: This course will enable students to complete a research project within their given specialisation in readiness for examination. Students will further develop their knowledge to resolve their research project. Students will further develop research, critical reflexivity and communication skills through the development of an honours thesis (written thesis, or artefact and exegesis) (Part B).
learning_outcomes: Develop the results of a preliminary investigation into a resolved research project
Collate and critically evaluate relevant data
Communicate a developed knowledge in their selected topic or area
Justify intrinsically or extrinsically the procedure(s) followed and articulate the rationale for research and methodology used
Synthesise developed knowledge in relevant theories and apply related research skills
Make informed and justified decisions to support final presentation/installation, including in selection, editing, and finish
Present a logically structured argument that is theoretically sound and convincing
prerequisites: Must have completed all of CREA1008 Research Practices (Creative)/CREA5000 Research Methods (Creative)
incompatibilities: Must not have completed CREA4003 Honours Research 3 (Creative) at the University of South Australia

title: Urban Design for Health and Sustainability
school: School of Arch and Built Env
syllabus_overview: Urban Design for Health and Sustainability course provides learners with an understanding of the interrelationship between urban design, public health, and sustainability, emphasising key principles and processes involved in urban design, with a specific focus on enhancing sustainability and public health. Through this course, learners will gain the knowledge and skills to critically evaluate various urban design strategies, examining their effectiveness in creating cities that are both environmentally sustainable and conducive to the well-being of their inhabitants. The course will also enable students to analyse real-world examples of successful urban planning practices, identifying key factors that contribute to the development of healthy, liveable, and resilient urban spaces. By combining theoretical insights with practical applications, the course prepares students to make informed decisions about urban design, empowering them to create urban environments that promote health, sustainability, and quality of life for diverse communities.Learning activities include case study analysis, tutorial exercises, and both collaborative and individual design-based assessments.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the key concepts link between urbanisation, urban design, public health and sustainability

Demonstrate a critical understanding of the urban design theories and principles along with analytical and practical approaches to create sustainable and healthy development in urban and regional context.
Apply urban design theoretical framework, concepts and guidelines to assess and develop healthier, more resilient and sustainable urban spaces at different scales and for different settings.
Perform a detailed appraisal of an urban development site/s using broader urban health and sustainability goals

title: Curatorial and Museum Studies Research Thesis
syllabus_overview: This course is a supervised research thesis of 20,000 words to be undertaken in the field of Curatorial and Museum Studies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate specialist knowledge in the area of their research.
Demonstrate the ability to initiate research and to formulate viable research questions.
Demonstrate the capacity to design, conduct and report sustained and original research.
Demonstrate the ability to evaluate scholarly literature.
Present research findings in a suitably structured thesis that conforms to protocols of academic presentation and research practice.
Demonstrate the ability to critically assess literature and conduct analyses at a Masters level.
prerequisites: Must have completed at least 48 units of study
incompatibilities: Must not have completed MUSEUM7003 Curatorial and Museum Studies Research Thesis at the University of Adelaide

title: Effects Element Development

In this course, students will develop skills in working within the digital effects production pipeline. Students will undertake production projects to develop familiarity and expertise with key dynamic effects development techniques including importing attributes, casting, and dynamics simulations. By the end of the course, students will have acquired the skills required to produce industry standard dynamic effects sequences.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard dynamic effects production practices
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality dynamic effects simulations
Demonstrate autonomy and adaptability in planning and managing a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline through iterative project submission and review
Demonstrate direction within a simulated team environment and produce work that meets industry-standard quality assurance and review processes
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM5075-Effectss Element Development at the University of South Australia

title: Jazz Performance 1A
school: Elder Con Mus & Sch Perf Arts
syllabus_overview: Specialisations are offered across a range of instruments, as well as voice. Students receive 11 hours per semester of individual tuition in their chosen specialisation. Through the study of appropriate technical studies and jazz repertoire, students develop advanced technical proficiency alongside a strong understanding of jazz style and interpretative principles. Students are expected to perform their selected repertoire with accuracy and fluency, demonstrating secure rhythmic control and a well-developed creative and expressive voice. They must also demonstrate jazz improvisation in appropriate styles, a strong conceptual understanding of the works performed, and the ability to communicate effectively with an audience.
learning_outcomes: Exhibit technical and musical skills that, through accuracy, fluency and stylistic awareness, illustrate a strong and maturing conceptual and interpretative understanding of the student's instrument and chosen repertoire
Exhibit effective practising strategies which arise from independent, imaginative and creative approaches to problem solving including the use of contemporary technologies
Manifest critical understanding of the performance standards required for professional endeavour and an ability to assess one's own performances and those of fellow musicians
Exhibit skills in performance etiquette, communication and interaction with an audience
Exhibit curiosity, self-awareness and problem-solving skills that will enable continuous learning and growth
incompatibilities: Must not have completed MUSJAZZ1001 Jazz Performance 1A at the University of Adelaide

title: Museum Internship
syllabus_overview: This course provides hands-on practical experience working in a museum or art gallery. Interns will work within a professional setting and learn from industry specialists. Internship projects may relate to any area within museums such as curatorship, marketing, public programs, object or collection significance assessment, research, and fundraising. Internships will be negotiated together with the course convenor.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of museum industry best practice.
Demonstrate the ability to work as a team to achieve an outcome.
Develop new skills in museum and art gallery practice.
Show an understanding of a range of issues concerning care, storage and display of objects and artworks.
Show an understanding of the range of professional skills and proficiencies required to work within a cultural institution.
prerequisites: Must have completed LIBR5003 Making a museum OR must have completed LIBR5005 The Secret Life of Objects: Museums in Practice
incompatibilities: Must not have completed MUSEUM7004 Museum Internship at the University of Adelaide

title: Look Development and Lighting
syllabus_overview: This immersive industry based course, delivered on-site at Rising Sun Pictures, will build upon students’ existing visual effects knowledge, and familiarises students with professional practice in the visual effects industry, providing the theory, skills, and techniques to produce industry-standard dynamic effects simulations. In this course, students will undertake a series of advanced production projects that will emulate the processes of a professional production schedule. Students will be required to extend their effects and lighting skills in order to produce a high quality, finished project for inclusion in their showreel, and to be presented to peers and RSP staff at the end of the course. By the completion of the course, students will have acquired the skills required to produce industry standard photorealistic dynamic effects sequences.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and implement industry-standard dynamic effects and lighting production practices
Apply key tools and techniques within industry standard software to generate professional quality photorealistic dynamic effects simulations
Demonstrate autonomy and adaptability in planning and managing a program of work to meet a production brief and its deadline through iterative project submission and review
Demonstrate direction within a simulated team environment and produce work that meets industry-standard quality assurance and review processes

title: Electricity Market and Power System Operations
school: School of Elec and Mech Eng
syllabus_overview: This course provides a broad knowledge of the wholesale electricity market and power system operation in terms of energy and ancillary services. It includes the evolution of the power system industry and electricity market over time, rules and regulations, energy and ancillary services markets and transmission system operation with a focus on the Australian Electricity Market.
learning_outcomes: Describe the evolution from vertically integrated utilities to deregulated electricity markets, explain market architectures and participant roles, and apply microeconomic principles including supply-demand modelling, market equilibrium, welfare economics, pricing schemes, and market power to electricity market analysis.

Develop mathematical optimisation models from fundamental concepts, including linear programming (LP), mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), and quadratic optimisation, interpret duality and shadow prices, and implement solutions using GAMS and MATLAB with optimisation solvers.

Formulate and solve economic dispatch (ED) problems including multi-period ED with ramp limits, multi-objective ED with emissions considerations, energy storage modelling, and value of lost load analysis.
Formulate and solve optimal power flow (OPF) problems using AC and DC formulations, estimate network losses, and develop security-constrained and network-constrained unit commitment (UC) models.
Describe ancillary services products and procurement mechanisms, explain contingency analysis fundamentals, and analyse the co-optimisation of energy and ancillary services in spot markets.

Evaluate the impacts of intermittent renewable resources on electricity market operations, analyse renewable generation prediction and participation mechanisms, examine market operation under uncertainty, and identify the roles of new market participants such as virtual power plant operators.
prerequisites: Must have completedENGEX419Electrical Power Systems
corequisites: If not the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled inENGEX419Electrical Power Systems
incompatibilities: Must not have completed ELEC ENG 4087, ELEC ENG 7087 at University of Adelaide

title: Secondary Science for Teaching 1
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to build preservice teachers’ understanding of the nature of scientific knowledge and the purpose of teaching science in the secondary school context. The course examines the impact of learning theories on the teaching of science and explores approaches to assessment and teaching methodologies appropriate for secondary science. Preservice teachers will encounter ways of using the laboratory in science teaching and gain a comprehensive understanding of the Australian Curriculum and how it informs science teaching and learning.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on personal and professional assumptions of the nature of science taught in schools
Select, critique and apply strategies for teaching science in the middle years
Identify strategies to identify and challenge alternative conceptions in science
Observe and analyse teacher practice
Effectively plan science lessons that are appropriate for particular contexts and purposes, including safe and appropriate use of laboratory equipment
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUCX237 Science for Secondary Teaching 1 OR must not have completed EDUC2088 Science Curriculum 1 at the University of South Australia

title: UO Radio and Audio Journalism
school: School of Comm, Media and Jour
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to further develop students' ability to write for radio, longer format radio stories and podcasts. Students will build on existing knowledge of broadcast writing and producing. Students will develop skills to edit news stories using industry-standard software, compile news reports, apply industry standards to news writing, voice reporting, news production and podcasting as well as knowledge of sourcing and interviewing techniques. They will identify and analyse key ethical and legal obligations associated with broadcast reporting including podcasting.Students will experience the practical constraints of radio journalism and will learn to work to daily deadline pressures in a team.
learning_outcomes: apply developed ability in writing for radio (news/current affairs/podcasting)
use technology associated with radio production and editing
develop competence in radio writing, reporting, producing and podcasting
critically interpret current issues reported in Australian and international broadcast media outlets
identify key ethical and legal obligations associated with radio reporting and podcasting
prerequisites: Must have completedJOUR1004News Writing OR must have completed JOUR1009 UO News Reporting
incompatibilities: Must not have completed COMM2106 UO Radio and Audio Journalism at the University of South Australia

title: Chinese IIB
syllabus_overview: This course is a continuation of Chinese IIA. It consists of tuition in speaking, listening to, writing and reading modern standard Chinese. This course further extends students' knowledge of basic grammar, vocabulary and structures found in the spoken and written forms of contemporary Chinese. The main emphasis is on building up vocabulary and reading experience as a basis for studying contemporary Chinese society and culture. It is anticipated that by the end of the course students will know around 900 Chinese characters and most commonly used Chinese grammar patterns.
learning_outcomes: acquire knowledge and understanding of the basic vocabulary and grammar
develop skills in reading and comprehending essays in Chinese on topics covered in the course
construct, write and type sentences and short texts in Chinese on the topics covered in the course
apply basic skills to use paper references and online resources for studying Chinese language independently
develop interpersonal and communication skills through group/peer discussion and assignment in both Chinese and English
be more aware of the different ways of seeing the world through cultural/social issue topics in the course

Be more aware of cultural respect, differences and diversity and will have more knowledge and understanding of the issues involving intercultural communication and develop culturally appropriate manner with Chinese native speakers

title: Science for Secondary Teaching 1
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to extend preservice teachers' critical understanding of the nature of scientific knowledge and the purpose of teaching science in the secondary school context. Students will critically examine learning theories, evaluate research on science education and curriculum frameworks, and design, justify and evaluate inquiry-based and laboratory learning experiences for diverse learners across the secondary years.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine personal and disciplinary assumptions about the nature of science, drawing on science education research and theoretical perspectives to inform curriculum thinking
Critically evaluate and apply strategies for teaching science in the middle years, justifying pedagogical choices in response to learner needs and contexts.
Analyse the origins and persistence of alternative conceptions in science, developing evidence-informed strategies to identify and address them.
Observe, analyse and interpret science teaching practice, connecting observed approaches to evidence on student learning and providing informed feedback to peers.
Design, justify and evaluate science learning experiences that are contextually appropriate, inclusive and grounded in principles of inquiry and safe laboratory practice.

title: Journalism Foundations
school: School of Comm, Media and Jour
syllabus_overview: To enable students to develop an understanding of principles, practices, contexts and issues in contemporary Australian and international journalism. This introductory course offers knowledge about the purposes and forms of journalism produced in Western and non-Western media systems, and what journalism can achieve locally, regionally, nationally and internationally. It covers recent developments in the practice and focus of journalism, and features specialist and cross-cultural reporting, such as First Nations journalism. Students will also develop foundational skills of ethical journalistic practice and storytelling, including story sourcing, researching, interviewing, and writing.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the roles and purposes of journalism in Western and non-Western settings, and of fundamental elements of media literacies
Develop and apply journalism knowledge and practical skills to source, research, interview for, and write journalism texts
Identify key legal and ethical obligations associated with journalism
Demonstrate an appreciation for the social, political, historical and commercial contexts in which journalism operates and the ways in which these influence journalism
Apply the principles of clear, grammatical written expression in accordance with the program’s style guide and academic writing and referencing requirements
