There is recognition of reductionist thinking and its benefits and disadvantages; systems thinking and complexity are discussed; several system methodologies and Senge's system dynamics provide a context and specific skills. Major topics addressed include Network of essentially systems; Emergence; Self-organisation; Systems design; Systemic structure; Systems tools; Mental models; Path history; Systemic and cascading risk and events; the Environment driving system scope and structure; Dynamism; Sense making and common meaning; Identifying leverage points; Systems intelligence.
learning_outcomes: Identify what a complex system is and how they differ from simple and complicated systems
Use key aspects of complex systems and the benefits of particular approaches in managing complexity
Recognise whether a proposed system or project should be primarily in a controlled space or in the innovation space on the edge of chaos in order to gain the benefits
Recognise the benefits of system dynamics and its use in identifying leverage points in systems
Apply these advanced and uncommon skills to address societal problems
Investigate international best practice
prerequisites: must have completed PROJX500 Project Management Fundamentals

title: Program and Portfolio Management
syllabus_overview: This unit specifically addresses how organisations deliver strategic goals and objectives through the selection of a balanced Portfolio and Programs of multiple Projects. This selection balances the needs of 'business as usual' with the need to be disruptive or face disruption in a rapidly changing market. This unit outlines how participants can gain competence in managing this balance of today's requirements with tomorrow's needs. Specifically, this unit will address how an organisation strategically applies management techniques to select, initiate, prioritise, executes and controls initiatives through Portfolio Alignment, Monitoring and Control. The course will also consider how an organisation can benefit from delivering multiple projects in a Program environment including governing, controlling and supporting the organisation's strategy through Program Management. The course objective is to build participants competence in managing portfolios and programs.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate portfolio needs and apply advanced principles of portfolio managementfor portfolioprioritisation process in line with industry standards
Critically analyse and synthesize the nature of program management, its focus on benefits realisation, and the inter-relationship between program components in depth
Establish the high-level governance, including risk management, for successful achievement of portfolio and program outcomes through understanding of stakeholders' needs and influence
Demonstrate advance personal development and leadership & communication skills in group work
Demonstrate deep commitment to ethical, social and cultural issues and their importance for project managers for career progression to program and portfolio managers
prerequisites: must have completed PROJX500 Project Management Fundamentals

title: Managing Organisational Development and Change
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip you with advanced knowledge to support a comprehensive understanding of organisational change principles using established and emerging theories, models, technological tools, and practical strategies, to initiate and manage organisational development and change. You will be equipped to design and implement organisational change initiatives, develop leadership and stakeholder strategies, and foster innovation, agility, ethics, and sustainability; and will be enabled to evaluate change impact using frameworks that support continuous improvement and long-term organisational success.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability, both individually and in teams, to apply organisational development and change theories and models, using established and emerging approaches, and technological tools, to diagnose, design and plan organisational change.

Effectively communicate, critically evaluate, and apply change management strategies that integrate leadership principles, and stakeholder management techniques, to facilitate successful organisational change in a dynamic global context.
Integrate key organisational culture and agility principles to develop actionable, innovative, ethical and sustainable change initiatives.
Critically assess the impact of change initiatives using appropriate evaluation frameworks that support continuous improvement and long-term organisational effectiveness.

title: Foundations of International Business
syllabus_overview: Foundations of International Business is a comprehensive course designed to provide graduate students with a foundational understanding of the global business landscape. Through an exploration of global business environments and the opportunities, challenges and risks they present, students will develop the essential tools needed to navigate the complexities of international business management.The course covers a wide range of topics essential for success in the international arena, including regionalization, globalization, and the role of multinational enterprises. Students will explore theories of trade and foreign direct investment, gaining insights into conducting sustainable businesses in diverse political, economic, and socio-cultural systems. Furthermore, they will examine the impact of economic development and social change on international business operations.By the end of the course, students will be equipped with the knowledge, skills, and diverse perspectives necessary to excel as international business managers in today's interconnected global economy
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical concepts and analytical tools to address managerial problems in international business
Understand, explain and analyse the complexity and diversity of the international business environment
Recognise global issues and discuss their implications for international business
Critically analyse and interpret information as well as international economic and political developments for sustainable managerial decision-making
Communicate and present analytical findings and strategic recommendations in relation to international business operations of a firm

title: Risk Assessment and Management
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with an in-depth understanding of risk management methodologies and processes applicable to project environments. It examines risks throughout all stages of the project lifecycle. The course covers an array of interconnected theoretical concepts with practical techniques, encompassing various methodologies, uncertainty management, risk identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment. It also covers risk management tools and techniques, project risk knowledge management, and lessons learned. This course aligns with the program intent to provide a comprehensive understanding of project management knowledge and skills to prepare learners to manage project uncertainties in an innovative, ethical and sustainable way.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced risk management theories, methodologies and technical standards to real-world scenarios across various project lifecycle
Critically evaluate complex problems in project risk management context, proposing actionable innovative, ethical and sustainable solutions
Make high-level, independent judgments across a range of technical and managerial aspects of project risk management
Apply advanced communication skills to effectively convey and discuss complex project risk management information with diverse stakeholders
Use advanced individual and team skills to contribute constructively to team with demonstrated leadership and strategic thinking

title: Marketing for Tourism, Events and Hospitality
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to allow students to gain and apply knowledge in the area of experiential tourism and marketing. The course will enable students to analyse travel behaviour, identify market opportunities to design an innovative experiential product, and propose a bespoke marketing strategy. The course will emphasise links with other courses in program through case studies of effective marketing strategies for tourism, events, and hospitality. The course content and assessment will foster graduate qualities such as problem-solving and communication skills and ability to propose innovative and sustainable solutions for the industry.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate opportunities for existing and new experiential travel, events, and hospitality products based on research of global and local market trends
Critically analyse travel motivations and behaviour to identify viable target markets
Propose a creative experiential product that responds to identified market opportunities and travel needs
Devise an appropriate marketing strategy for the implementation of a proposed product
Apply relevant theories to idea generation and implementation strategy
Communicate devised strategies in a variety of formats, as appropriate for industry and academic audiences

title: AI for Business
syllabus_overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the world, it is impacting every industry and is forecast to be a multi-trillion dollar industry by the end of the decade. Many of the world's largest companies, including Microsoft, Google, Facebook and Amazon, heavily utilise AI throughout their businesses to outpace their competitors. But what is Artificial Intelligence? And how can it be leveraged to improve a business? This course aims to answer these questions through exploring the types of AI that exist, how AI is currently being used to create value within businesses, and how this transformative technology can be implemented effectively to create new products and services. Throughout the course we will also explore the practical implementation challenges alongside the societal, economic and ethical questions that arise when applying AI in business.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish the different types of AI and how they are applied in a business context
Identify the different types of datasets and data sources and how they can be leveraged to gain strategic advantage with AI
Assess an organisation's existing data sources and business processes to identify opportunities to gain strategic advantage using AI
Analyse and develop implementation strategies for AI solutions in business contexts, considering viability, scalability, and organisational readiness
Communicate the social, economic and ethical implications of applying AI in real world applications

title: People Analytics
syllabus_overview: This course develops students’ advanced knowledge of the role of analytics in the context of HRM through the application of analytics-based tools to address complex HR issues, including ethical and legal implications. People Analytics approaches are increasingly important in today’s business context. In this course, students discuss key HR questions, apply analytics-based tools to analyse and evaluate information, and create reports. This course also delves into debates around the ethical issues associated with the use and misuse of analytics and employee data and devises a strategy for applying People Analytics in the organisation. Students are assessed through case study and data analysis.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and apply statistics to analyse data and inform Human Resource decisions

Apply statistical analysis techniques, such as correlation and regression analysis, to evaluate data and develop solutions for common Human Resource challenges such as diversity management, employee turnover, and job performance by utilising the statistical outcomes and relevant Human Resource theories and concepts
Create data visualisations using statistical software and communicate findings suitable for reports to stakeholders
Critically evaluate and assess complex ethical issues associated with people analytics to produce strategic recommendations

title: Project Procurement and Contract Management
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip learners with advanced and integrated knowledge and skills to plan, execute, and manage procurement and contract activities throughout a project lifecycle. Students will explore various theoretical concepts and practical procurement processes, including procurement planning, solicitation methods, procurement and contracting strategies, tendering procedures, drafting specifications, evaluation techniques, ethical procurement practices, and the application of contract law. The course also covers contract administration, closeout procedures, supply chain management, and strategies for resolving contract disputes. This course aligns with the program’s intent to provide advanced understanding and technical skills necessary for effective project management.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate advanced procurement and contract management processes throughout a project lifecycle and implement them in real-life scenarios to optimise project outcomes.
Critically analyse complex project procurement and contractual issues and propose innovative and actionable solutions.
Apply advanced procurement knowledge and techniques to develop a comprehensive project procurement plan that respects cultural diversity and considers sustainability and ethical factors.
Demonstrate advanced communication skills to effectively articulate procurement and contract management concepts, information, and decisions to diverse stakeholders.
Show leadership and team management skills in tasks that require negotiating, collaborating, and leading within the context of project procurement and contract management.

title: Complex Project Management
syllabus_overview: This course is intended to help students better prepare for managing complex projects in the current and future business worlds, characterised by emergence and uncertainty. A variety of relevant theories and tools are covered, including systems theory, systems thinking, and the concept of an evolving toolbox for complex project management. Real-life complex project management case studies are discussed in the context of the various domains, including air, maritime and urban transportation, construction, infrastructure, and disaster recovery. Topics include modelling and simulation, adaptability, agility, resilience, project scheduling, systemic risk management, and failure mode effects and analysis.
learning_outcomes: Identify different types of projects in project management and explain how management styles can vary depending on the type of a project employed
Analyse real life complex project management case studies from multiple domains and illustrate practical application of research methods and toolsets
Examine the latest interdisciplinary research in complex project management and apply lessons learned and best practices to the development of potential solutions to contemporary global challenges
Compare and employ different levels of interpersonal skills as appropriate for effective teamwork and leadership in complex project management
Demonstrate the importance of developing broader awareness and maintaining high ethical and socio-cultural standards to successful complex project management
prerequisites: must have completed PROJX500 Project Management Fundamentals

title: Business Decision Making and Problem-Solving
syllabus_overview: This course is designed to equip students with knowledge and skills in decision making and problem solving within a contemporary business context.It aims to provide practical tools and frameworks for addressing complex business challenges in both routine and crisis situations, in improving decision quality, and fostering innovative solutions to meet organisational goals.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess ambiguous and multi-dimensional problems using structured problem-framing techniques to distinguish root causes from symptoms across business contexts.
Explain and critically discuss the implications and effect of cognitive biases, groupthink, and ethical issues on decision making.
Critically examine and integrate traditional and innovative methodologies techniques, and tools, in a systems thinking approach to generate, evaluate, and prioritise ethical solutions.

Demonstrate skills in problem solving and decision making as an individual and in teamwork to evaluate various decision-making frameworks, models and tools, and critically explain the most appropriately selected approach in applying to a real-world problem.

title: Entrepreneurial Business Development
syllabus_overview: This course prepares postgraduate students to lead innovation and entrepreneurial initiatives across diverse contexts—startups, corporations, social enterprises, and academic spinouts. It delivers a deep exploration of business development, entrepreneurial innovation programs, customer-centric thinking, and strategic commercialisation. Through a 12-module sequence, students apply lean and agile methodologies, map innovation ecosystems, and develop real-world entrepreneurial proposals aligned with stakeholder needs and strategic objectives.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and assess entrepreneurial opportunities using innovation and market-based frameworks.
Design, test, and iterate business development and innovation programs aligned with strategic goals.
Apply customer discovery techniques and segmentation to refine business models.
Demonstrate foundational skills in pricing, negotiation, positioning, and buyer engagement
Develop and present compelling entrepreneurial proposals and pitches
Reflect on personal entrepreneurial strengths and team collaboration capabilities

title: Project Leadership
syllabus_overview: Effective project leadership involves more than having a good project plan and telling people what to do. It involves effectively engaging with your team to provide them with the resources and the environment to care about and deliver the project results. You will analyse different models of leadership, which attempt to explain how some leaders are successful, and their characteristics. Students will consider how their own personality style affects the way they work with others and in teams. Interpersonal awareness, skilful communication and relationship building are key skills to building and guiding a high performing team. Good leaders are aware of the context of their project leadership in their organisation, cultural differences and internal organisational dynamics, which can affect performance. We explore how people management systems within organisations structure the way leaders can manage and influence staff to achieve project outcomes within legal and ethical requirements. This interactive course combines theory with practical experience.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and apply advanced leadership theories with particular reference to project teams within an organisation

Apply advanced leadership theories to recognise their personal work and interpersonal styles and how they impact on the project team and sponsors and identifying areas for their personal professional development
Demonstrate high level competence in interpersonal relations to effectively communicate with and influence their colleagues within formal settings
Synthesise deep knowledge of relevant theories, governance processes, and ethical responsibilities to address contemporary leadership issues within organisations

title: People, Leadership and Organisational Performance
syllabus_overview: To provide students with theoretical knowledge and practical application of organisational behaviour, leadership, and management, exploring and critically appraising different forms in varying organisational, cultural, and industry settings. Discuss and appraise the relationship between an organisation's culture, its leadership, and its employees and develop strategies for managing performance.
learning_outcomes: Acquire critical thinking and problem solving skills to improve the management of one's self, others, and teams at work
Evaluate management theories for personal development, improved effectiveness and address the `knowing' and `doing' gap in managing people and organisations
Develop skills to evaluate and produce ethical, responsible, and global perspectives and actions within self, coworkers, leaders, and organisations
Analyse the challenges and opportunities facing organisations, managers, teams, and employees through the principles of organisational behaviour and scientific enquiry

Demonstrate Business Enterprise Skills: i) Self-Management (intermediate level); ii) Ethical Awareness (intermediate level); iii) Teamwork (intermediate and advanced levels); iv) Written Communication (intermediate level); and iv) Oral Communication (intermediate and advanced levels) *NOTE: Only Teamwork and Oral Communication are assessed for AoL Accreditation purposes

title: New Venture Creation
syllabus_overview: This course is aimed at exposing the students to modern approaches to new venture creation; placing the entrepreneurial team at the centre of the process. It is designed for anyone who needs to assess and develop potential business or project opportunities that are mainly, but not exclusively, based on a technological concept or a social innovation. Screening techniques are introduced that will address the new venture value proposition: including analysis of the underlying business concept, the base technology, benefits to customers, and fit with potential markets. Models for new venture development which include consideration of the resourcing requirements, team development and future strategies will be treated in depth; and a comprehensive model for new venture validation will be developed during the course.
learning_outcomes: Identify the difference between a business idea and a potential innovative business opportunity
Articulate a new venture value proposition and communicate ideas and concepts effectively
Build an assessment process for a new venture to determine its desirability, feasibility, viability, and sustainability
Develop practical strategies for exploiting business opportunity and resourcing new venture creation and development
Prepare a comprehensive validation for a potential new venture of your own design and recommend future strategy

title: Leading New Product Innovation
syllabus_overview: This course will provide you with the capability to use theory, frameworks and techniques to develop, experiment and evaluate potential innovative ideas to stay relevant and drive growth in the modern consumer landscape. Through experiential workshops, you’ll cultivate a future focused, flexible innovation mindset. You’ll learn to address biases, embrace change, and foster an innovation-friendly environment within an organisation. The course will teach you to identify key innovation drivers and leverage customer research, internal resources, and company culture to differentiate your organisation in competitive markets. It’s ideal for those leading new product innovations in tech startups or corporate settings.
learning_outcomes: Summarise, justify and explain key underlying factors that form an effective product innovation process
Develop and lead innovation that will consider ethical, social and environmental impact, culture and diversity in the creation and progressive development of new product innovations
Critically analyse and evaluate new product ideas in order to prioritise potential to address key innovation lenses and technology requirements
Create and communicate a value proposition to solve a market problem

title: Digital Innovations in Tourism, Events and Hospitality
syllabus_overview: Information has been described as the lifeblood of tourism, with information and communication technologies (ICT) playing a key role in tourism management and operations. With digital innovations driving and fostering radical change in the sector, enabling firms to streamline operations, increase productivity, enrich customer service and enhance competitiveness, understanding how to leverage and manage technology-based innovations has become a critical issue. Adopting a management, as opposed to a technical, approach, this course aims to develop your management skills and competencies in exploiting information and computer technologies within the broad tourism sector, as well as anticipating their revolutionary impacts on three major tourism stakeholders: tourism demand; tourism suppliers; and tourism destinations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the transformative impact of digital developments on customers, organisations, and destinations within tourism, hospitality and events.
Interpret the role of digital in enriching tourism experiences, enhancing business operations, and developing new tourism offerings.
Demonstrate the ability to use managerial skills to exploit digital to improve the performance and competitiveness of tourism firms and destinations.
Demonstrate critical analytical skills in predicting and managing technological change and innovation in tourism.

title: Strategic People Management
syllabus_overview: This course deepens students’ understanding of the links with social and cultural diversity and its impact on organisations, strategic people management, managing change and performance. This course takes an overarching look at the people management system of an organisation. It introduces students to some key concepts in human resource management and organisational behaviour. It also provides students an opportunity to critically analyse popular people management techniques. Finally, students will get an opportunity to evaluate real world situations involving people in organisations and develop realistic solutions. Students are assessed through a report, debate and problem solving exercise.
learning_outcomes: Assess the alignment of an organisation’s strategy to their human resource strategy, structure and human resource system design to ensure organisational performance and growth
Investigate strategic human resource challenges and develop solutions using an evidence-based approach
Evaluate the design of human resource management system of an organisation taking dynamic changes in the internal organisational context and external operating environment into consideration

Critically reflect on ethical and social justice issues associated with human resource management activities and recommend solutions taking the rights and the interests of different stakeholders into consideration
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, written and oral communication, and the ability to apply an international perspective to inform stakeholders and implement change

title: Digital Supply Chains
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with fundamental concepts and latest developments in digital tools and technologies in supply chains. It develops their knowledge of digital supply chains, including the digitalization of manufacturing, warehousing, logistics and procurement as well as the performance of the system. In this course, the effects of digitalization on supply chain operations are studied to give students a fuller understanding of the dynamics and factors involved in the emergence and growth of digital supply chains. This course also investigates the opportunities and challenges of managing digital supply chains in today’s highly competitive global business environment. Students are assessed through a case study, presentation and report.
learning_outcomes: Explain the concept of digital supply chains and how they emerged and grew over time.
Describe and explain the impact of digitalization on present and future supply chains.
Identify and critically analyse the opportunities and challenges of managing digital supply chains in the highly competitive global business environment.
Critically evaluate the performance of digital supply chains.
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, written and oral communication, teamwork, and applying global perspectives digital supply chains.

title: Strategy
syllabus_overview: This course focuses on the importance of strategic management in determining organisational performance by introducing the management concepts, skills and abilities relevant to an organisation's strategic capacity to create and capture value and succeed in competitive environments. Students will learn about and critically apply contemporary strategic management concepts, frameworks and tools. Topics include an integrated approach to applying tools and frameworks to strategic analysis, formulating strategy and strategy implementation.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the complex organisational environments in which businesses operate using relevant theories, concepts, and models
Individually and collaboratively evaluate and synthesize information and existing knowledge from multiple sources and experiences
Apply appropriate tools, theories, and concepts to analyse strategic issues in organisations and develop realistic options for implementation
Diagnose environmental forces and internal competencies/resources that drive and constrain strategic options for businesses
Participate constructively in team situations to complete tasks and meet agreed deadlines

title: Supply Chain Design and Analytics
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the strategic principles and analytical methodologies essential for designing and optimising efficient and resilient supply chain networks. This course delves into the intricacies of supply chain design, exploring key concepts, advanced analytics tools, and industry best practices. In this course, students develop advanced knowledge of the critical role of data analytics in supply chain design and management and how it can align and contribute to an organisations overarching strategic goals and objectives.
learning_outcomes: Understand the role of supply chain design and analytics in optimising operations
Apply optimisation models and simulations to design efficient networks
Leverage data analytics for optimising supply chain metrics
Apply analytics concepts to real-world case studies
Demonstrate problem solving, communication, teamwork, and global perspectives

title: Managing Employee Performance and Rewards
syllabus_overview: This course develops students critical understanding of how organisations define, assess, reward, and manage employee performance within contemporary and global work environments. It examines the strategic role of performance management systems and reward practices in influencing employee behaviour and organisational outcomes by focusing on both theoretical insights and practical applications.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a clear understanding of performance and reward management theory and practices and their role in the context of organisational and HR strategy in the global business environment.

Critically analyse complex performance and reward management issues in an organisation and develop actionable, innovative, ethical and sustainable recommendations that maximise individual and team performance.
Critically evaluate the impact of contemporary issues on performance and reward management.
Demonstrate advanced level communication, both individually and within teams, to engage a range of stakeholders.

title: Event Leveraging and Legacy
syllabus_overview: The course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills for strategic event management, optimising the benefits of hosting events through event legacy and leveraging. By expanding upon foundational concepts of event management, the course explores the enduring benefits of event legacies and strategies to utilise events as catalysts for positive changes. Designed to enhance critical thinking and analysis skills crucial for strategic use of events, the course prepares students to excel in any field related to event management or involvement.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the diverse event legacies on host societies
Recommend approaches to enhance legacies for a broader range of communities and individuals
Propose event leveraging activities to maximise the benefits of hosting events
Develop strategies to achieve successful and sustainable event outcomes

title: Australian Industrial Relations
syllabus_overview: This course develops students' advanced knowledge of the theory and practice of Australian industrial relations, including the parties or stakeholders, social processes, institutional arrangements, outcomes, and their inter-relationships. Both the theoretical and practical aspects of industrial relations (IR) or employment relations (ER) are explored. The employment relationship is regulated by rules, which are created and enforced through particular social processes involving tripartite actors—employees and their representatives, employers and their associations, and the State or government who interact with each other within the IR/ER system. Students are assessed through problem solving exercises that require them to solve real-life IR/ER problems.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the range of theoretical and analytical perspectives within industrial relations/employment relations.
Critically evaluate the structures, institutions and practices shaping industrial relations/ employment relations at the workplace, industry and economy-wide level.
Identify and explain the Australian industrial relations/employment relations laws, regulations, practices and procedures in both formal study and practical application.

Explain the main steps in establishing, amending, terminating and utilising individual and collective workplace agreements, as well as awards, in the context of federal legislation and relevant court decisions.
Understand and apply the values or frames of reference in industrial relations/employment relations.
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, ethical awareness, written and oral communication, respecting cultural diversity, and applying global perspectives.

title: Research Topics in Procurement and Supply Chains
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with knowledge and understanding of special issues and the latest developments in procurement and supply chain management. In this course, students study different procurement and supply chain research problems and approaches and gain insights into the current and future directions of research in the field. This course enables students to critically analyse and evaluate research approaches and problems in procurement and supply chain management as well as recommend evidence-based, that is, research-supported solutions.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse procurement and supply chain research approaches
Appraise and evaluate procurement and supply chain research problems
Compare and contrast alternative solutions to procurement and supply chain problems
Recommend research-supported solutions to procurement and supply chain problems
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, oral and written communication, teamwork, and applying global perspectives

title: Strategic Management of Human Resources
syllabus_overview: This course develops students advanced knowledge and skills of the theory and practice of contemporary strategic human resource management (SHRM). Many organisations undergo constant change, many of which require the adoption of new work practices and new approaches to decision-making and performance management. In many of these organisations, HR people have been leaders in identifying the organisation's particular challenges and in finding and implementing solutions. This course delves into the important links between HRM functions and the organisations overarching strategic goals and objectives. Students are assessed through an essay as well as a presentation and report.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine and analyse the evolution, practice and theoretical interpretations of Strategic HRM
Analyse and apply recent innovations in strategic HRM theory and practice
Undertake an environmental and organisational assessment and propose organisationally appropriate HR strategy and operational practices
Demonstrate use of appropriate communication techniques to a variety of audiences
Understand the ethical and international dimensions of the practice of strategic HRM, and integrate this awareness into the practice of strategic HRM
Demonstrate skills in working independently and autonomously

title: Consumer Behaviour and Insights
syllabus_overview: This course introduces the theory of consumer behaviour and relates it to the practice of marketing. It will present relevant material drawn from psychology, anthropology, social and behavioural sciences within the framework of the consumer decision process and its main influencing factors.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and explain factors which influence consumer behaviour and how knowledge of consumer behaviour can be applied to marketing practice.
Apply empirical generalisations and models that describe consumer behaviour patterns.
Report on theoretical and practical aspects of consumer behaviour using real world examples.
Synthesise information and existing knowledge from a number of sources and experiences while displaying critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
Explain the nature and scope of consumer behaviour and address this through individual and team work.

title: Leadership: Self and Others
syllabus_overview: This course aims to enhance the student’s ability to understand leadership and develop their own leadership practice; to engage the people they lead and develop their own personal and organisational productivity through increased self-awareness and reflection on their personal leadership capabilities, enabling students to make informed and effective decisions related to the people management in the workplace. This course includes the analysis of different models of leadership, interpersonal awareness, skilful communication and relationship building, how people management systems within organisations structure, and how leaders can manage and influence staff to achieve project outcomes within legal and ethical requirements.
learning_outcomes: Critically assess students’ own leadership potential
Formulate the evidence-based strategies and plans to improve leadership practices
Develop a clear understanding of the evidence-based approach to leadership practices
Analyse and compare leadership requirements for the growth of self and others

title: Veterinary Public Health Rotation
school: School of Animal and Vet Sci
syllabus_overview: The Final year rotation will see the DVM III students build on their DVM II Veterinary Public Health experience. The rotation will include components that can be delivered online.Students will be exposed to a variety of theoretical and practical activities to achieve Day One competency in Veterinary Public Health. This may include activities performed in association with laboratories, Primary Industries and Regions SA, South Australian Research and Development Institute, Department of Agriculture, abattoirs and other food and meat processing facilities. They will also do case work with academics in areas of VPH/One Health. Some weekend and out of hours work may be expected within the rotation.Topic Definition: Veterinary Public Health has been defined by Food and Agricultural Organisation of the United Nations, World Health Organisation/ World Organisation for Animal Health as 'the sum of all contributions to the physical, mental and social well-being of humans through an understanding and application of veterinary science'. Veterinary Public Health thus embraces the following areas of knowledge: diagnosis, surveillance, epidemiology, control, prevention and elimination of zoonosis and of diseases that threaten food security and social cohesion; protection of food (including meat and milk) for human consumption; food and meat science; environmental protection; animal welfare standards; and the social, behavioural and mental aspects of human-animal relationships.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Day One Competencies for the discipline of Veterinary Public Health in clinical reasoning / problem solving / knowledge.
Demonstrate the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Day One Competencies for the discipline of Veterinary Public Health in technical skills.
Demonstrate the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Day One Competencies for the discipline of Veterinary Public Health in communication skills.
Demonstrate the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Day One Competencies for the discipline of Veterinary Public Health in project management.
Demonstrate the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Day One Competencies for the discipline of Veterinary Public Health in professional behaviours.
prerequisites: Must have completed Must have completed all of Year 2 of the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine
incompatibilities: Must not have completed VET SC7305ARW Veterinary Public Health Rotation A and VET SC7305BRW Veterinary Public Health Rotation B at the University of Adelaide AND must not have completed all of VETS6018 Veterinary Public Health Rotation A/VETS6019 Veterinary Public Health Rotation B

title: Nutrition Metabolism
school: School of Ag, Food and Wine
syllabus_overview: This course explores connections between nutrition in early life and its impact on our metabolism, physiology, and healthy ageing. A healthy start to life is critical and nutritional imbalances early in life can increase chronic disease risk. We are living longer, and this comes with an additional set of nutritional challenges. The aim of this course is for students to investigate how early life nutrition impacts future chronic disease risk and how nutrition and metabolism are linked with healthy ageing. Students will also explore how our genetic makeup contributes to healthy ageing and explores the feasibility of personalised nutrition.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the physiological and genetic mechanisms controlling macronutrient metabolism.
Discuss the role of human diet on metabolism, and physiology.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the interrelated roles of nutrition, genetics and metabolism for the prevention and treatment of chronic disease.
Critically evaluate nutritional health information communicated to the public.
Explain the role of metabolism and nutritional health in healthy aging.
Demonstrate professional communication skills across a range of delivery modes.

assessment_tasks.task_name: Assessment Plan, Media Task, Multiple Choice Questions

title: Strategic Procurement
syllabus_overview: The aim of this course is to critically analyse and develop a strategic response to issues related to procurement and supply management. It explores the nature of strategic and sustainable procurement in both the public and private sectors, providing students with the opportunity to challenge their understanding of procurement’s role within an organisation and its supply chains.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles, competencies, and strategic approaches to procurement and supply management.
Critically evaluate sourcing decisions, local and global sourcing, and supplier relationships demonstrating multi-institutional perspectives.
Critique procurement governance, sustainability risks, and emerging technologies providing actionable innovative and ethical solutions.
Develop a strategic sourcing plan for manufacturing and service operations that addresses a complex supply management problem.

title: Project Management Research Project
syllabus_overview: This course asks students to undertake a capstone research project in respect to a topic of their choice as aligned to project management. The content covered includes reviewing published literature, building on research methodology knowledge, addressing the topic via qualitative or quantitative secondary research data and drawing conclusions in respect to research outcomes. Students will need to apply the skills required to develop a research proposal, presentation and final report based on extending current knowledge.
learning_outcomes: Research a significant issue within project management.
Identify and critically analyse relevant research topic information.
Synthesise the industry findings and articulate them.
Document the research processes in a research report.
prerequisites: Must have completedECON6000Research Methods and Development

title: Environmental and Resource Economics and Applications
syllabus_overview: This course applies the critical thinking and practical reasoning of economic analysis to the management of environmental and natural resources and examines the role of economic theory in understanding and solving environmental and resource problems. Domestic and international empirical evidence will illustrate real-world applications and implications. There will be a strong focus on topical policy issues, such as, air and water pollution, species loss, single-use plastics, renewable and non-renewable resource management (fisheries, forests, and minerals), and the impact of trade. A key assessment component will involve students undertaking a significant policy project regarding a topical resource or environmental issue.
learning_outcomes: Apply economic analysis to the management of the environment and natural resources
Analyse theoretical and empirical research in environmental and natural resource economics
Explain how relevant economic theory and empirical applications can be used to address contemporary environmental and natural resource issues
Demonstrate good inter-personal and communication skills in the application of economic analysis to environmental and natural resource issues
incompatibilities: Must not have completed ECON7016 Resource & Environmental Economics PG at the University of Adelaide

title: Strategic Value Chains
syllabus_overview: This course equips students with the expertise to design, analyse, and optimise value chains, leveraging cutting-edge tools and technologies to create and capture value. In today’s interconnected and competitive business landscape, effective value chain management is vital for organisational success. Through a dynamic blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students will develop strategic thinking and decision-making skills to align value chains with organisational goals, boost competitiveness across diverse industries, and thrive in both domestic and global markets.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the strategic importance of value chains in achieving organisational objectives and competitive advantage in global markets
Analyse value chain processes and integration, to identify and propose technologically innovative opportunities for optimisation and improvement

Develop, justify, and present value chain strategies in high-functioning teams, aligning with organisational goals and responding to market dynamics, while demonstrating advanced communication, leadership, and cross-cultural collaboration

Assess the impact of technological advancements and global trends on value chain design and management, designing strategic solutions to future-proof organisations while communicating findings effectively

title: Biotechnology in Practice
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the processes and requirements involved in developing and manufacturing a biomedical consumable within a biotechnology company. It explores key considerations in product development, from initial research to production. Working in groups, students will design a product development plan and apply Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) principles. These principles will be demonstrated through a small-scale, in-house production case study. The skills and knowledge gained in this course will be highly applicable to students’ future careers in biotechnology.
learning_outcomes: Outline the research and development processes involved in the commercialisation of biotechnology products, including the importance of intellectual property (IP) considerations.
Evaluate the principles of quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) in biotechnology commercialisation.
Apply biotechnology commercialisation principles and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) in small-scale biotechnology product manufacturing.
Communicate research, development, and manufacturing concepts in biotech commercialisation both individually and collaboratively.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed BIOTECH 7007 - Biotechnology in Practice (UoA) at The University of Adelaide

title: Strategy in the Age of Digital Disruption
syllabus_overview: Students undertaking this course will develop an in-depth understanding of strategic principles and their application to generate solutions to complex and unpredictable strategic problems characterised by new technologies and innovations. The course introduces participants to the theories, frameworks and concepts underlying modern strategic management, highlighting its utility in an environment being revolutionised by digital disruption. Leveraging the Analysis-Formulation-Implementation approach, it provides participants with the orientation, perspectives, and competencies needed to manage organisations in business environments characterised by monumental and rapid change to outperform competitors in the long term.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate a broad range of strategy principles, concepts, tools, and frameworks for application in strategic management within the defence and space sectors.
Recognise how organisations successfully develop and execute strategies that lead to sustainable competitive advantage.
Evaluate the effects of the ongoing digital revolution on strategic management and business practices.
incompatibilities: must not have completed BUSS5454 Strategy in the Age of Digital Disruption at the University of South Australia

title: Negotiation
syllabus_overview: This course develops students' advanced knowledge of the theory and practice of negotiation, including the processes and subprocesses, strategies and tactics that can be applied to achieve mutually beneficial agreements. This course combines collaborative and individual exercises that are theoretical and practical. These exercises allow students to reflect on negotiation experiences and outcomes and develop a reflective praxis, which are essential to constructing knowledge around negotiations and their dynamics as real-life phenomena. By adopting a problem-solving approach, this course gives students competencies and skills to understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, and develop negotiation plans, which are grounded in robust preparation and research. Students are assessed through a project and reflection.
learning_outcomes: Apply, analyse and evaluate the theory underlying negotiation, including conciliation and mediation.
Understand and apply the skills involved in forming strategy, planning and researching for negotiations.
Apply, analyse and evaluate skills in the practice of workplace negotiations, face-to-face or online, including for individual and collective agreement making in employment relations.
Communicate clearly and research effectively individually and collectively or cooperatively.
Reflect on negotiation knowledge and its application to real-life situations and develop a reflective praxis.
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, ethical awareness, written and oral communication, respecting cultural diversity, and applying global perspectives.

title: Ethics, Sustainability and Governance
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with theoretical and practical knowledge to analyse, and implement solutions to ethics, sustainability, and governance challenges in the global environment. By evaluating concepts and knowledge in the specific areas of business ethics, sustainable business practice, and corporate governance, this course will enable learners to develop skills in complex problem-solving, decision-making, and professional ethics across diverse cultures and international business contexts. This course aligns with the program’s intent to equip students to think critically and apply higher order analytical and problem-solving skills in international perspectives for their prospective clients or employers.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the theoretical and practice-based theories of ethics, sustainability, and governance, and the impacts these have on management and leadership.
Identify and analyse ethical issues and apply appropriate knowledge and problem-solving skills to recommend solutions for such issues.
Investigate social and environmental sustainability issues and propose sustainable business practices.
Critically review cross-cultural issues, their implications on business, and develop competencies to recommend strategies including Corporate Social Responsibility.
Apply principles of corporate governance to organisational management and leadership in the context of sustainability in business environments.

title: Global Food and Nutrition Science Capstone Project A
school: School of Ag, Food and Wine
syllabus_overview: This is a Capstone Course in the Master of Science (Global Food and Nutrition Science), building upon learnings from the first year of study in the Master of Science (Global Food and Nutrition Science). Each student will work on a research or industry related project, in conjunction with an experienced supervisory team in their field. Skills within a research and industry setting will be developed along with written and oral communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Communicate scientific findings in a food or nutrition area concisely in written and spoken English
Demonstrate mastery of the techniques required for the experimental study of a research question related to food or nutrition science
Demonstrate a critical approach in evaluation of the current state of knowledge in an area of research within food and nutrition science
Develop a rigorous and methodical approach to the maintenance of records and the collection, storage and analysis of collected data
corequisites: Must be enrolled in SCIE4001 Research Methods and Data Analysis
incompatibilities: Must not have completed FOOD SC 7035AWT at The University of Adelaide

title: Education Policies and Systems
syllabus_overview: The history of education and educational philosophy will be analysed in terms of the impact on educational policy in schooling, training and/or higher education in contemporary times and in the future. Policy will be critiqued through many frameworks to understanding the complicated relationship between policy and practice and the implications for educators at the level of curriculum, pedagogy and assessment. The process of informing, shaping, implementing and evaluating educational policy will also be explored in the context of change and educational reform. The course will examine educational policy from ethical, sociological, cultural, international, comparative and historical perspectives.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the philosophical assumptions of education policy
Critique contemporary issues in diverse education systems and the way they intersect with education policy at the local, national and international level
Evaluate the strengths and limitations of the education policy development process
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7550 Education Policies and Systems at the University of Adelaide

title: Project Management Fundamentals
syllabus_overview: This course aims to equip learners with advanced theoretical and practical knowledge necessary for managing projects across various stages of the typical project lifecycle. It covers a wide range of principles, skills, and techniques essential for effective project management, including project management systems and generic concepts, project management processes and techniques, processes integration, project environment, and the roles of the project management. This course aligns with the program’s intent to provide a deep understanding of the key Project Management standards for management of projects of various scales and industry sectors.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced theoretical and technical knowledge of project management processes across a typical project lifecycle.
Critically analyse, evaluate and transform project management principles in order to generate creative solutions to complex problems in professional scenarios.
Make high-level, independent judgments across a range of technical and managerial functions within the project management context, selecting applicable tools and techniques for project management.
Apply advanced communication skills to effectively covey and discuss complex project management information and ideas with diverse stakeholders.
Use advanced individual and team skills to contribute constructively to team with demonstrated leadership and strategic thinking.

title: Economics Curriculum & Pedagogy (UG)
syllabus_overview: The focus of this course and its companion Curriculum and Pedagogy is learning and teaching theory and its application in practice for teaching. This includes planning, developing and assessing learning for diverse student cohorts in line with the Australian and SACE Curriculum requirements in this subject specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate deep knowledge and understanding of the concepts, substance, and structure of the content area and the complexity of the discipline teaching strategies in the learning area.
Design and sequence unit and lesson plans based on essential content of the subject area, curriculum and assessment principles.
Demonstrate understanding of assessment, moderation, and its application to support consistent and comparable judgments of student learning
Integrate relevant research and theory to develop a broad repertoire of subject-appropriate teaching and learning strategies, including the use of ICT
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC4113 Economics Curriculum & Pedagogy (UG) at the University of Adelaide

title: Advanced Marketing Analytics
syllabus_overview: To provide students with the theoretical and operational tools of marketing analytics for decision making at the advanced level. Students will explore the intricacies of marketing analytics. They will develop the skills and knowledge needed to extract meaningful insights from data and drive effective data-driven strategies.
learning_outcomes: Apply and explain advanced marketing analytics tools to interpret data from various sources
Communicate complex marketing analytics findings effectively to both specialist and non-specialist audiences
Evaluate empirical data to evaluate business growth patterns across different industries and countries and identify key factors influencing these patterns
Translate the results of quantitative analyses into managerial insights for marketing decision-making to solve strategic and tactical problems

assessment_tasks.task_name: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis

title: Sustainability, Risk and Governance
syllabus_overview: This course explores the interconnections between sustainability, corporate risk management, and governance. Students will learn to integrate sustainable practices into business models, assess environmental and social risks, and develop governance frameworks that promote ethical practices and long-term sustainability.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the evolution of business responsibility as it relates to current and future operations.
Analyse and apply sustainability frameworks and standards as they relate to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks in business operations.
Apply stakeholder theory to critically evaluate complex issues in current business operations.
Develop recommended enhancements to business practices grounded in ethical and sustainability principles.

title: Languages Education
syllabus_overview: This course aims to explore pedagogies for working with children from different language backgrounds and working with the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support teachers of languages and the teaching of languages in early childhood and primary settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify the languages and cultures knowledges children and young people bring to learning sites, their relationship to concepts of self, identity, community and place, and how these impact learning

Analyse languages education policy, frameworks and curricula, including the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support learners’ plurilingual capabilities and languages inclusion in classrooms and sites
Apply strategies and pedagogies to promote language development and learning in linguistically and culturally diverse sites, centres and classrooms

title: Global Food and Nutrition Science Capstone Project B
school: School of Ag, Food and Wine
syllabus_overview: This is a Capstone Course in the Master of Science (Global Food and Nutrition Science), building upon learnings from the first year of study in the Master of Science (Global Food and Nutrition Science). Each student will work on a research or industry related project, in conjunction with an experienced supervisory team in their field. Skills within a research and industry setting will be developed along with written and oral communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Communicate scientific findings in a food or nutrition area concisely in written and spoken English
Demonstrate mastery of the techniques required for the experimental study of a research question related to food or nutrition science
Demonstrate a critical approach in evaluation of the current state of knowledge in an area of research within food and nutrition science
Develop a rigorous and methodical approach to the maintenance of records and the collection, storage and analysis of collected data
prerequisites: Must have completed FOOD6003 Global Food and Nutrition Science Capstone Project A

title: Qualitative Methods in Social Research
syllabus_overview: This course introduces students to the various traditions, methodologies, and methods that inform qualitative research. Qualitative research helps researchers access deep aspects of lived experience and can address some of the elusive why questions of social life. Qualitative research highlights the complexity and richness of social life, which is typically inaccessible to large-scale social surveys. Students will encounter a wide range of qualitative research methods and perspectives, for example, feminist perspectives, symbolic interactionism, ethnography, discourse analysis, and qualitative interviews. Students will have the opportunity to test out some of these methods and will also develop skills in qualitative research design.
learning_outcomes: Identify the strengths and limitations of qualitative research, and when it is especially valuable to engage in qualitative inquiry
Discriminate between different qualitative methodologies and methods
Conduct qualitative fieldwork and produce a qualitative research report
Demonstrate the ability to align research questions with qualitative methods and methodologies and justify the appropriateness of this alignment

title: Wellbeing for Positive and Inclusive Communities
syllabus_overview: Wellbeing, safety and inclusion are increasingly seen as a significant issue in educational settings. Schools and school systems are challenged to improve the quality of care offered to students. This course focuses on contemporary issues in wellbeing, safety and inclusion education worldwide. Students will explore current developments and trends in wellbeing, safety and Inclusion and its impact on schools and schooling. Students will also analyse and evaluate how wellbeing and inclusion education can help create flourishing communities. Upon completing this course, students will have critical knowledge and understanding of current themes of wellbeing, safety and inclusion literature and be able to critique wellbeing interventions.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate contemporary issues in wellbeing, safety and inclusion education
Analyse and evaluate how wellbeing, safety and inclusion education creates flourishing communities
Compare and contrast the efficacy of different wellbeing, safety and inclusion approaches to creating positive wellbeing outcomes
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC5236 Learner and Educator Wellbeing for Positive Communities at the University of South Australia

title: Mixed Methods Research
syllabus_overview: This course offers an introduction to both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, delving into theoretical perspectives and practical methods. The primary focus is to equip students with the knowledge and skills to discern the appropriateness of various basic qualitative and quantitative techniques and apply these to the collection and analysis of research data. Through critical examination, students will gain the ability to evaluate the relevance of these approaches in designing their own research endeavours. The course is divided into two halves with the first focusing on quantitative methodologies and the second on qualitative methodologies.
learning_outcomes: Understand the theoretical and conceptual underpinnings of qualitative, quantitative and mixed-methods research.
Determine appropriate qualitative and quantitative methodological approaches in relation to specific educational problems.
Demonstrate competency in collecting, organising and analysing both qualitative and quantitative data.
Present and discuss the findings of qualitative and quantitative research to different audiences in a variety of formats.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC7065 Mixed Methods Research at the University of Adelaide

title: Learning, Memory and Education
syllabus_overview: This course aims to explore the role of memory in education, focusing on contemporary research and practice, sensory, short-term, working and long-term memory, as well as memory retention and its implications for learning and teaching.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the different types of memory (sensory, short-term, working, and long-term) to understand their specific roles and functions in educational settings
Evaluate evidence-based memory strategies to determine their effectiveness in improving student learning outcomes
Synthesise contemporary research and practice on memory and learning to develop innovative teaching approaches

title: Innovations in Food Processing
school: School of Ag, Food and Wine
syllabus_overview: This course aims to allow learners to develop an advanced knowledge and understanding of the processing and engineering principles of food production systems. Content will include discussions on heating, cooling, freezing, drying, crystallisation, extrusion technology, fermentations, fractionation, non-thermal technologies and kinetics of physico-chemical changes during processing. Learners will also be able to communicate the outcomes of food processing systems to a wide range of audiences. The focus will be on innovative and current technologies currently in use or being developed in the food industry.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the importance of food processing
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of innovative processing technologies
Discuss the role of new and emerging food innovation technologies
Analyse the effects of processing on food products
Communicate the outcomes of different food processing strategies to a technical and general audience
incompatibilities: Must not have completed FOOD SC 7031WT at the University of Adelaide

title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation
syllabus_overview: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the nature of enterprise and entrepreneurship and introduces the role of the entrepreneur, innovation, and technology in the entrepreneurial process. Students will gain the theoretical and practical knowledge of entrepreneurship and innovation, and explore their impact on organisational management and leadership, business strategy, and business conduct.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on theoretical and practice-based principles of entrepreneurship and innovation, and the implications these have for organisational management and leadership.

Critically evaluate the market and the competitive conditions for an entrepreneur, an innovation or a new technology to ground a market-driven new venture concept within the context of a newly formed venture, existing small to medium size growth-oriented venture, or an entrepreneurial venture within a larger corporation.

Apply principles of entrepreneurship and innovation to develop an innovative business concept within the context of a stand-alone start-up, a corporate venture, a social enterprise, or a family business.
Demonstrate effective written and oral communication of an innovative business concept within a context of a stand-alone start-up, a corporate venture, a social enterprise, or a family business.

title: Digital Learning Design and Implementation
syllabus_overview: This course aims to extend pedagogic understanding and practices of digital learning to the design and implementation of innovative digital learning approaches, artefacts, and applications.
learning_outcomes: Apply digital learning concepts, models and practical strategies to guide, construct and reflect on pedagogical approach
Analyse and evaluate learning technologies for the achievement of appropriate pedagogical outcomes
Design and develop a digital learning experience that utilises appropriate and relevant technologies
incompatibilities: Must not have completed EDUC5242 Digital Learning Environments Design and Implementation at the University of South Australia

title: Advanced Microscopy Imaging and Analysis
syllabus_overview: This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of microscopy techniques and their practical applications in the field of biomedical research. Through hands-on training, students explore cutting-edge advancements in sample preparation, imaging and data analysis, and apply their new skills to authentic research scenarios. Upon completion of the course, students will have a deep understanding of the principles and applications of a range of microscopy technologies. By working in teams to design and carry out microscopy experiments, students will build on their collaborative problem-solving and communication skills, that are essential for future career success. This course aligns with the programs goal of preparing graduates for making impactful contributions to commercial biotechnology research.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles and processes behind current microscopy techniques used in biomedical research and the biotechnology industry.
Apply knowledge of current and key microscopy techniques to address real life challenges.
Successfully perform laboratory skills required for a range of microscopy techniques, including sample preparation, imaging, and image software analysis.
Critically interpret and analyse experimental data relating to microscopy.
Effectively communicate microscopy-related concepts, adapting the communication mode according to audience and purpose.
incompatibilities: Must not have completed BIOTECH7009 at The University of Adelaide

Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions

title: Learners in a Digital Age: Innovative Practices
syllabus_overview: To critically analyse current global trends in learning with digital technologies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of digital technology on learners and learning
Analyse a range of contemporary technologies and the trends of development
Analyse how social justice is impacted by technology
